definition_zh: 草坪；草地
definition_en: an area of short cut grass, especially around a house
core_image: 一片修剪整齐的绿草，边缘还留着割草机压出的条纹
scene: 清晨的院子里，草叶上还挂着露水。 He spent the morning mowing the lawn.
sceneCN: 这里是「草坪」（第 1 个义项：修剪过的草地）；句意为他花了一上午修剪草坪。图中可辨识物件：带露水的草叶、割草机、院墙。

derivatives.zh: 由 lawn 与 mower 复合，义为「割草机」
由 lawn 加 -y 构成，义为「像草坪的；多草的」

senses.title: An area of cut grass
senses.definition: a piece of ground covered with short, regularly cut grass, especially near a house
senses.definitionCN: 一块覆盖着修剪整齐的短草的地面，尤指房屋附近
senses.example: He spent the morning mowing the lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了一上午修剪草坪。
senses.why: Lawn began as a word for a clearing or open glade; once people kept such grass short, the word moved to the mown ground itself.
senses.whyCN: lawn 最初指林中空地，后来人们把这种草地保持得很短，词义就转到修剪过的草地本身。

senses.title: A fine linen fabric
senses.definition: a fine, light linen cloth used for shirts and handkerchiefs
senses.definitionCN: 一种精细轻薄的亚麻布，用于衬衫和手帕
senses.example: The collar was made of crisp white lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 衣领是用挺括的白色细麻布做的。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different place name and a different history; it is a look-alike that English spelled the same way.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个地名和另一段历史，是英语中拼写碰巧相同的同形词。

intro.en: Lawn meaning grass comes from a word for a clearing; lawn meaning fine linen comes separately from the French town of Laon.
intro.cn: 表示「草坪」的 lawn 来自「林中空地」一词；表示「细麻布」的 lawn 则另来自法国城市拉昂。

items.en: Lande meant a heath, moor or open clearing, a piece of land without trees.
items.cn: lande 意为荒地、荒原或林间空地，指没有树木的一片地。

items.en: The French word is often traced to a Gaulish root for heath or open ground, but the evidence is not conclusive.
items.cn: 这个法语词常被追溯到高卢语中表示荒地或空地的词根，但证据并不充分。

items.en: Middle English launde names a glade or open grassy space.
items.cn: 中古英语 launde 指林间空地或多草的开放空间。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the sense narrows to ground kept short by mowing.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，词义收窄为靠修剪保持短草的草地。

items.en: Modern English lawn means the garden grass, while the linen sense survives separately from Laon.
items.cn: 现代英语 lawn 指庭院草坪，而细麻布义则另从拉昂的地名独立留存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words formed from lawn and its history; the near-meaning group gathers ground covered with grass.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lawn 及其历史形成的词；近义组收覆盖草的地面。

entries.definition: A machine used to cut grass.
A light chair for sitting outdoors.
A Middle English word for a glade or open ground.
entries.definitionCN: 中古英语中表示林间空地的词。

entries.definition: The green plants that cover the ground.
Short grass and the soil under it.
A piece of grassy ground, especially in a village.
A field of grass and flowers.

normalIntro.en: The garden word and the linen word are two histories that happen to share a spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 草坪词与麻布词是两段恰好共享拼写的历史。

normal.en: Lawn for grass is related to land and glade, not to the linen.
normal.cn: 表示草坪的 lawn 与 land、glade 有关，与麻布无关。

normal.en: Mow the lawn is the fixed phrase for cutting it.
normal.cn: mow the lawn 是「修剪草坪」的固定搭配。

normal.en: Lawnmower joins lawn and mower in one word.
normal.cn: lawnmower 把 lawn 与 mower 合成一个词。

normal.en: The linen lawn is named after Laon in France.
normal.cn: 细麻布 lawn 得名于法国城市拉昂。

normal.en: Lawns takes -s in the plural: two lawns, front and back.
normal.cn: 复数加 -s：two lawns，前后两块草坪。

abstract.en: A word for wild clearing became a word for a carefully kept square of grass.
abstract.cn: 一个表示荒野空地的词，变成了精心维护的一方草地。

abstract.en: Two unrelated histories can hide behind one spelling, and only context separates them.
abstract.cn: 两段无关的历史可以藏在同一个拼写后面，只有上下文能把它们分开。

abstract.en: A lawn is nature kept at a chosen length, a small argument between growth and the mower.
abstract.cn: 草坪是被维持在选定长度的自然，是生长与割草机之间的一场小争论。

examples.en: He spent the morning mowing the lawn.
examples.cn: 他花了一上午修剪草坪。

examples.en: The children ran across the front lawn.
examples.cn: 孩子们跑过前院草坪。

examples.en: The collar was made of crisp white lawn.
examples.cn: 衣领是用挺括的白色细麻布做的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「隆」——草地长得隆隆一片，就是 lawn。

root: 表示草坪义来自古法语 lande（荒地、空地），更早一般追溯到高卢语；细麻布义另来自法国地名 Laon。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a kept-short grassy ground; a second, unrelated sense names a fine linen.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是维护得很短的草地；另一个无关义项指一种细麻布。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square of green grass with mower stripes still visible along its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一方绿草，边缘还留着割草机的条纹。

branches.en: a striped lawn seen from a kitchen window
branches.cn: 从厨房窗里看见的条纹草坪

branches.en: a mower turning at the edge of the grass
branches.cn: 在草地边缘转弯的割草机

branches.en: a white collar folded on a shirt
branches.cn: 衬衫上折好的白领

branches.en: a handkerchief thin enough to see light through
branches.cn: 薄得透光的手帕

branches.en: one spelling, two unrelated histories
branches.cn: 一个拼写，两段无关的历史

intro.en: The grass word is a French-derived stem; its family grows by compounding, and the linen word is a separate place name.
intro.cn: 草坪词是法语来源的词干，同族靠复合扩展；麻布词则是另一个地名。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: one who or that which mows

definition_zh: 热带的；炎热的（如热带般闷热的）
definition_en: belonging to the hot regions near the equator, or as hot and humid as those regions
core_image: 雨林里巨大的叶片垂着水珠，藤蔓从高树一直挂下来
scene: 雨林的午后，空气闷得像浸过水，宽大的叶子仍在滴水。 The garden is full of tropical plants from South America.
sceneCN: 这里 tropical 是「热带的」（第 1 个义项：属于赤道附近炎热地区的）；句意为园中满是来自南美的热带植物。雨林里滴水的大叶和藤蔓，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 tropical 去掉后缀构成，义为「热带地区」
tropical 的词根名词，义为「回归线；热带」
由 sub-（副）与 tropical 复合，义为「亚热带的」

senses.title: Near the equator
senses.definition: belonging to the belt of the earth that lies near the equator and is always warm
senses.definitionCN: 属于地球赤道附近终年温暖的那一带
senses.example: The garden is full of tropical plants from South America.
senses.exampleCN: 园中满是来自南美的热带植物。
senses.why: Greek tropos, a turn, named the line where the sun turns back, and the whole belt took that name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 tropos（转向）命名了太阳折返的那条线，整条地带也随之得名。

senses.title: Weather that feels like it
senses.definition: used of weather that is hot and damp even far from the equator
senses.definitionCN: 形容即使远离赤道也又热又潮的天气
senses.example: The air was tropical for a week after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后有一周空气都闷热得像热带。
senses.why: A heat that hangs and does not dry out copies the feeling of the equator, so any such day may be called tropical.
senses.whyCN: 那种悬着不散的湿热复制了赤道的感觉，于是这样的日子也被称作 tropical。

intro.en: Tropical belongs to the noun tropic, which comes from the Greek tropos, a turn, because the sun appears to turn back at the tropics.
intro.cn: tropical 属于名词 tropic，后者来自希腊语 tropos（转向），因为太阳在回归线处看起来折返。

items.en: Tropos meant a turn or a way of turning, from trepein, to turn.
items.cn: tropos 意为转向或转向的方式，出自 trepein（转）。

items.en: The adjective tropicus was used of the solstice, the sun's turning point.
items.cn: 形容词 tropicus 原用于至日，即太阳折返的时刻。

items.en: The two tropics were named as the lines where the sun turns back each year.
items.cn: 两条回归线得名于太阳每年折返之处。

items.en: English tropic named the lines, and tropical described the whole hot belt between them.
items.cn: 英语用 tropic 指这两条线，tropical 形容它们之间整条炎热的地带。

items.en: The word then extended to hot, damp weather anywhere and to storms born in that belt.
items.cn: 这个词进而扩展指任何地方的湿热天气与诞生于该地带的风暴。

note.en: The first group shares the trop stem, the second holds other words for heat and climate zones.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trop 词干，第二组收其他表示炎热与气候区的词。

entries.definition: The hot belt around the equator.
Either of the two turning lines of the sun.
Of the line around the middle of the earth.
Hot and damp in a heavy way.
Carrying a lot of water in the air.

normalIntro.en: Tropical is tropic plus -al, and tropic comes from a word for turning, because the sun turns back at those lines.
normalIntro.cn: tropical 是 tropic 加 -al，而 tropic 出自表示「转」的词，因为太阳在那些线上折返。

normal.en: Trop means turn, so the tropics are where the sun turns back.
normal.cn: trop 意为转，所以热带是太阳折返的地方。

normal.en: The adjective simply adds -al to tropic.
normal.cn: 形容词只是在 tropic 后加 -al。

normal.en: The tropics is always plural for the region itself.
normal.cn: 指整个地区时 tropics 总是复数。

normal.en: Sub in front gives subtropical, just outside the belt.
normal.cn: 前面加 sub 得 subtropical，就在那带之外。

normal.en: Tropical fish live in warm water, not in the sea of the far north.
normal.cn: tropical fish 生活在温暖的水里，不在北方远海。

abstract.en: A leaf so large it holds a small pool.
abstract.cn: 一片大得能盛一小池水的叶子。

abstract.en: Air that feels like warm wet cloth on the face.
abstract.cn: 像热湿布贴在脸上的空气。

abstract.en: Vines hanging straight down from the high canopy.
abstract.cn: 藤蔓从高处树冠笔直垂下。

examples.en: Tropical rainforests hold more species than any other place on land.
examples.cn: 热带雨林所含物种比陆地上任何地方都多。

examples.en: Bananas and mangoes are examples of tropical fruit.
examples.cn: 香蕉和芒果都是热带水果。

examples.en: The coast was hit by a tropical storm in August.
examples.cn: 海岸在八月遭到一场热带风暴袭击。

dict_mnemonic.text: trop（转）＋ ical——太阳在这里折返，所以终年炎热，就是热带的。

root: 由 tropic 加 -al 构成，源自希腊语 tropē、tropos（转向）与拉丁语 tropicus，本指太阳折返的至日与回归线，后指其间炎热地带；同族词有 tropics、tropic、subtropical。

sensesIntro.en: First the belt near the equator, then the heavy heat that feels like it.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是赤道附近那条地带，再是像那条地带一样的闷热。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dripping leaf in the rainforest.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨林里滴水的宽叶。

branches.en: The geography branch: plants and animals of the belt.
branches.cn: 地理分支：那条地带的动植物。

branches.en: The weather branch: heat that hangs and will not dry.
branches.cn: 天气分支：悬着不散的湿热。

branches.en: The sunlight branch: both come from a high warm sun.
branches.cn: 阳光分支：两者都来自高悬的暖阳。

branches.en: The storm branch: storms born over warm seas.
branches.cn: 风暴分支：出生在暖海上的风暴。

branches.en: The imagination branch: any day can feel tropical.
branches.cn: 想象分支：任何一天都能感觉像热带。

intro.en: Tropical joins the Greek stem trop, a turn, with the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: tropical 把希腊词干 trop（转向）与形容词后缀 -al 结合起来。

latinIntro.en: The Greek root trepein, to turn, reached English through Latin tropicus, and the turning words below share it.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词根 trepein（转）经拉丁语 tropicus 进入英语，下面的「转」类词与它同源。

items.example: The stem explains the sun turning back.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干解释了太阳的折返。

items.example: It forms tropic, of the turning line.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tropic，与回归线有关的。
它由 tropic 构成 tropical。

items.example: The region takes a plural name.
Sub marks a zone just outside.
items.exampleCN: sub 标出紧邻在外的一带。

items.example: The adjective describes weather and life.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述天气与生物。

items.example: A plant turns toward light by tropism.

items.meaning: a prize for a turning of fortune
items.example: The old root also underlies the word for a prize.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老词根也支撑着表示奖品的词。

latinEntries.meaning: of the turning of the sun

definition_zh: 可靠的；可信赖的
definition_en: able to be trusted to do what is expected; giving consistent and accurate results
core_image: 同一座石桥几十年里每天承受同样的车流
scene: 河上那座石桥几十年如一日地承受着同样的车流，从没出过事。 We need a reliable source before we publish the story.
sceneCN: 这里 reliable 是「可靠的」（第 1 个义项：可以被信赖、按预期行事）；句意为在发表这篇报道之前，我们需要一个可靠的来源。画面里可留意：每天都承受车流的石桥。

senses.title: Able to be trusted
senses.definition: of a person or a thing, able to be depended on to do what is expected
senses.definitionCN: 指人或物能被依靠、按预期行事
senses.example: We need a reliable source before we publish the story.
senses.exampleCN: 在发表这篇报道之前，我们需要一个可靠的来源。
senses.why: The word is rely plus the ending able: what can be relied on is what can be leaned on without its giving way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 rely 加上词尾 able：能被 rely 的东西，就是可以靠上去而不塌的东西。

senses.title: Consistent in results
senses.definition: giving the same accurate result each time it is used
senses.definitionCN: 每次使用都给出同样准确的结果
senses.example: The old scale is not reliable enough for the laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧天平对实验室来说不够可靠。
senses.why: Trust in a machine is trust in repetition: the same result, again and again, without surprise.
senses.whyCN: 对机器的信任是对重复的信任：同样的结果一次次出现，没有意外。

intro.en: Reliable is rely plus able; rely itself goes back to a Latin verb meaning to bind fast, so the image is of something tied and able to hold.
intro.cn: reliable 是 rely 加 able；rely 本身可追到一个意为「绑紧」的拉丁动词，意象是被系住并能承重的东西。

items.en: Ligare meant to tie or bind, the root of ligament and of the relig- family.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆绑，是 ligament 与 relig- 词族的根。

items.en: Religare joined re-, back or fast, with ligare and meant to bind tightly.
items.cn: religare 由 re-（往回、紧紧地）与 ligare 组合，意为紧紧绑住。

items.en: Old French relier meant to bind together or to attach, and English borrowed it as rely.
items.cn: 古法语 relier 意为绑在一起或系上，英语借入后成为 rely。

items.en: English rely first meant to gather together, then to depend on a person or a thing.
items.cn: 英语 rely 最初意为聚拢，后来意为依靠某人或某物。

items.en: The ending -able turned the verb into an adjective of capacity: able to be relied on.
items.cn: 词尾 -able 把这个动词变成表能力的形容词：可以被依靠的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same binding stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of trustworthiness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「捆绑」词干的词；近义组收表示可信赖的形容词。

entries.definition: To depend on someone or something.
The state of depending on something.

normalIntro.en: The word is able to be tied to: what is reliable holds when you lean your weight on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「可以被系住的」：可靠的东西，在你把重量压上去时能撑住。

normal.en: Rely plus able: able to be depended on.
normal.cn: rely 加 able：可以被依靠的。

normal.en: A reliable source is one that has never had to be corrected.
normal.cn: a reliable source 是从来不需要更正的那种来源。

normal.en: A reliable car starts on cold mornings.
normal.cn: a reliable car 在寒冷的早晨也能发动。

normal.en: Reliability is measured over time, not in one good day.
normal.cn: 可靠性要靠时间衡量，不是靠一天的好表现。

normal.en: Ligare means to bind, and what is bound does not come apart.
normal.cn: ligare 意为捆绑，被绑住的东西不会散开。

abstract.en: Reliability is a promise kept more than once.
abstract.cn: 可靠，是被遵守了不止一次的承诺。

abstract.en: We trust machines for their repetition and people for their judgement.
abstract.cn: 我们因机器的重复而信任它，因人的判断而信任人。

abstract.en: A reliable witness is rarer than a loud one.
abstract.cn: 可靠的证人比声音大的证人更少见。

examples.en: We need a reliable source before we publish the story.
examples.cn: 在发表这篇报道之前，我们需要一个可靠的来源。

examples.en: The old scale is not reliable enough for the laboratory.
examples.cn: 这台旧天平对实验室来说不够可靠。

examples.en: She is the most reliable member of the night shift.
examples.cn: 她是夜班中最可靠的一员。

dict_mnemonic.text: rely（绑紧、依靠）加 able（能够）：能被系住、能靠上去的，就是可靠的。

root: 拉丁 ligare（捆绑）→ religare（紧紧绑住）→ 古法语 relier（绑在一起）→ 英语 rely（依靠）＋ -able → reliable；同族有 reliance、reliability、reliably，形近的 ligament 也出自 ligare。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being able to be leaned on; the senses move from a trusted person or source to a machine that repeats itself exactly.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「可以靠上去」；义项从可信的人或来源，到每次结果都一致的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone bridge carrying the same traffic for decades without a crack.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一座石桥几十年里每天承受同样的车流。

branches.en: a witness who never shifts
branches.cn: 说法从不动摇的证人

branches.en: a scale that gives the same reading
branches.cn: 每次读数相同的天平

branches.en: a person and a machine both predictable
branches.cn: 同样可预期的人与机器

branches.en: a nightly shift that always arrives
branches.cn: 每晚都准时到的人

branches.en: a story held back until it is checked
branches.cn: 核实之前压着不发的报道

intro.en: A Latin verb of binding gives a French verb of attaching, English makes it rely, and the ending of capacity turns it into an adjective of trust.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表「捆绑」的动词给出法语表「系上」的动词，英语把它变成 rely，表能力的词尾再把它变成表信赖的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is ligare, to bind; religare means to bind fast, and -able marks what can be done.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 ligare（捆绑）；religare 意为紧紧绑住，-able 标记「可以被……的」。

definition_zh: 附录；阑尾；附件
definition_en: a section of extra material added at the end of a book, or the small tube attached to the intestine
core_image: 书页末尾挂着的一小节补充内容，也像肠子上挂着的一根小尾巴
scene: 论文正文写完了，老师让他把调查问卷放在最后。 The questionnaire is in the appendix of her thesis.
sceneCN: 这里 appendix 是「附录」（第 1 个义项：书末的补充材料）；句意是调查问卷放在她论文的附录里。

derivatives.zh: 由 appendix 加表示炎症的 -itis 构成，义为「阑尾炎」
同根动词，义为「附加；贴上」
由 append 加名词后缀构成，义为「附属物；附件」
近义补充词，义为「补充（材料）」

senses.title: A section added at the end of a book
senses.definition: extra information placed at the end of a book or document, such as tables or questionnaires
senses.definitionCN: 放在书或文件末尾的补充信息，如表格、问卷等
senses.example: The full data tables are in the appendix.
senses.exampleCN: 完整的数据表在附录里。
senses.why: The Latin root pendere means to hang; an appendix is material that hangs at the end of the main text.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 pendere 意为「悬挂」；附录就是挂在正文末尾的材料。

senses.title: The tube attached to the intestine
senses.definition: the small closed tube joined to the beginning of the large intestine
senses.definitionCN: 连接在大肠起始处的一根封闭小管
senses.example: Doctors removed her inflamed appendix.
senses.exampleCN: 医生切除了她发炎的阑尾。
senses.why: The organ is also something that hangs off a larger part, so anatomy borrowed the same hanging image.
senses.whyCN: 这个器官同样是从较大部位上「垂挂」下来的东西，解剖学借用了同一个悬挂意象。

senses.title: A body part joined to a main structure
senses.definition: a smaller or less important part attached to a larger body or structure
senses.definitionCN: 附属于较大身体或结构的较小部分
senses.example: The tail is an important appendix in many animals.
senses.exampleCN: 尾巴是许多动物重要的附属部分。
senses.why: When something merely hangs on the outside of a structure, English reuses this word for it.
senses.whyCN: 当某物只是挂附在结构外部时，英语就复用这个词来称呼它。

intro.en: Appendix is Latin for 'something that hangs on', applied to book material and to an organ.
intro.cn: appendix 是拉丁语「挂附之物」，既用于书籍材料，也用于一个器官。

items.en: The reconstructed root *(s)pen- is generally taken to mean 'to draw, hang'.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *(s)pen- 表示「拉、悬挂」。

items.en: appendere meant to hang something on; appendix was the noun of result.
items.cn: appendere 意为把东西挂上去；appendix 是其结果名词。

items.en: appendix already meant an addition to a text.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中 appendix 已指文本的附加部分。

items.en: English borrowed it for book appendices.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入该词，指书末附录。

items.en: Anatomy applied the same word to the intestinal tube.
items.cn: 十七世纪解剖学把同一词用于肠上的小管。

items.en: Both the book sense and the organ sense are common today.
items.cn: 今天书附录义与器官义都很常用。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pend- hanging family; the near-meaning group gathers other add-on material.
note.cn: 形近组是 pend-「悬挂」词族；近义组是其他附加材料。

entries.definition: to add something at the end
a part joined to something larger
material added to complete or extend a text
a file or item joined to a main one
an addition to a document or building

normalIntro.en: An appendix hangs at the end, like a tag on a book.
normalIntro.cn: appendix 挂在末尾，像书后面挂着的标签。

normal.en: Append means to attach at the end; an appendix is what you append.
normal.cn: append 是附加，appendix 是附加出来的东西。

normal.en: Academic papers use the plural appendices.
normal.cn: 学术论文常用复数 appendices。

normal.en: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
normal.cn: appendicitis 是阑尾发炎，即阑尾炎。

normal.en: Refer to the appendix for the full data.
normal.cn: 完整数据参见附录，是论文常用说法。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-PEN-dix.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节：a-PEN-dix。

abstract.en: See a small pouch hanging at the end of a thick book.
abstract.cn: 想象厚书末尾挂着的小册子。

abstract.en: See a tiny tail hanging inside the body.
abstract.cn: 想象体内垂着的一根小尾巴。

abstract.en: See extra pages swinging behind the main text.
abstract.cn: 想象正文后摆动的附加页。

examples.en: The questionnaire is in the appendix of her thesis.
examples.cn: 调查问卷放在她论文的附录里。

examples.en: The full data tables are in the appendix.
examples.cn: 完整的数据表在附录里。

examples.en: Doctors removed her inflamed appendix.
examples.cn: 医生切除了她发炎的阑尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俄喷的」——像俄然喷出挂在书后的一截附加内容，附录。

root: 来自拉丁语 appendix「挂附之物」，由 appendere「挂上去」（ap- 去 + pendere 悬挂）派生；书末附录与体内阑尾都是「挂附」意象。

sensesIntro.en: One hanging image splits into extra pages at the end of a book and a small tube hanging in the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「悬挂」意象分成书末的附加材料和体内垂挂的小管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that hangs at the end of a larger whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：挂在更大整体末尾的东西。

branches.en: an appendix to the report
branches.cn: 报告附录

branches.en: refer to the appendix
branches.cn: 参见附录

branches.en: a burst appendix
branches.cn: 穿孔的阑尾

branches.en: appendix surgery
branches.cn: 阑尾手术

branches.en: the appendix of a crustacean
branches.cn: 甲壳动物的附肢

intro.en: A Latin hanging-family noun whose root also gives pend and suspend.
intro.cn: 这是拉丁「悬挂」词族的名词，同根词还有 pend 与 suspend。

latinIntro.en: Latin appendere combines ad- (towards) and pendere (to hang).
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 appendere 由 ad-（朝向）与 pendere（悬挂）构成。

definition_zh: 不足的；缺乏的
definition_en: not available in large enough amounts; difficult to find
core_image: 干旱的土地上，水桶里只剩下浅浅一层水
scene: 旱季里，干净的水变得稀缺。 Clean water is scarce during the dry season.
sceneCN: 这里 scarce 是「稀缺的；不足的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：旱季里干净的水很稀缺。

senses.title: Not enough in amount
senses.definition: existing in amounts too small for what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 数量太少，不足以满足需要
senses.example: Food was scarce after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后食物短缺。
senses.why: The core sense is a short supply of something needed.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是所需之物供应不足。

senses.title: Rare to find
senses.definition: uncommon and hard to find
senses.definitionCN: 不常见且难以找到
senses.example: Such birds are scarce in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟在这一带很罕见。
senses.why: A limited supply makes a thing uncommon.
senses.whyCN: 有限的供应使某物变得少见。

senses.title: In short supply
senses.definition: difficult to obtain because demand is higher than supply
senses.definitionCN: 因需求高于供应而难以获得
senses.example: Housing is scarce in the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 市中心住房供不应求。
senses.why: Economic shortage is the social form of scarcity.
senses.whyCN: 经济短缺是稀缺的社会形态。

intro.en: Scarce comes from Old French scars, from Latin excarpsus, plucked out.
intro.cn: scarce 源自法语古语 scars，更早来自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘除的）。

items.en: Excarpsus means plucked out or selected.
items.cn: excarpsus 意为被摘除或被挑出的。

items.en: Excerpere means to pick out or to take away.
items.cn: excerpere 意为挑出或拿走。

items.en: Scars meant sparing, limited, or hard to get.
items.cn: scars 意为节省的、有限的、难得的。

items.en: Scarce named a short supply of goods.
items.cn: scarce 指货物供应不足。

items.en: Scarce is central to economics and ecology.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scarce 是经济学与生态学的核心词。

note.en: Scarce is compared with similar spellings and with words for shortage.
note.cn: 把 scarce 与形近词以及表示短缺的词作比较。

entries.definition: a cloth worn around the neck
a mark left by a wound

normalIntro.en: Scarce and scarcity share a picture of empty shelves.
normalIntro.cn: scarce 与 scarcity 共享空货架的画面。

normal.en: A scarce item is like a shelf almost empty.
normal.cn: 稀缺的东西就像几乎空了的货架。

normal.en: Scarce adds ce to scar, but the sound is different.
normal.cn: scarce 比 scar 多了 ce，但读音不同。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun from scarce.
normal.cn: scarcity 是 scarce 的名词形式。

normal.en: Scarce resources are a basic idea in economics.
normal.cn: 稀缺资源是经济学的基本概念。

normal.en: Clean water becomes scarce in a dry season.
normal.cn: 旱季里干净的水会变得稀缺。

abstract.en: Scarcity forces people to choose.
abstract.cn: 稀缺迫使人们做出选择。

abstract.en: What is scarce often becomes precious.
abstract.cn: 稀缺之物常常变得珍贵。

abstract.en: A full world still has scarce clean air.
abstract.cn: 即使世界很满，干净空气仍然稀缺。

examples.en: Jobs are scarce in the small town.
examples.cn: 这个小镇的工作机会很少。

examples.en: Water grew scarce as the summer went on.
examples.cn: 随着夏天推移，水变得稀缺。

examples.en: The government must decide how to share scarce resources.
examples.cn: 政府必须决定如何分配稀缺资源。

dict_mnemonic.text: scarce 与 scarcity 同族，可联想「空空的货架」：需要的东西不够，就是 scarce。

root: 源自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘出的），经古法语 scars 进入英语，核心义「被取走大半、所剩无几」。

sensesIntro.en: Scarce means not enough, hard to find, or in short supply.
sensesIntro.cn: scarce 意为数量不足、难以找到，或供不应求。

core.en: A supply that is too small for the need.
core.cn: 相对于需求而言过于稀少的供应。

branches.en: The core state of not having enough.
branches.cn: 数量不足的核心状态。

branches.en: Rarity makes a thing hard to find.
branches.cn: 稀有使某物难以找到。

branches.en: Demand outruns supply in the market.
branches.cn: 市场中需求超过供应。

branches.en: Too little of something makes it uncommon.
branches.cn: 某物太少就会变得不常见。

branches.en: Rarity and high demand create shortage.
branches.cn: 稀有与高需求共同造成短缺。

intro.en: Scarce forms nouns and adverbs about shortage.
intro.cn: scarce 构成表示短缺的名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin excerpere, to pick out, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excerpere（挑出）是远源。

items.example: The scarceness of rain worried farmers.
Clean water is the scarcest resource.
items.exampleCN: 干净的水是最稀缺的资源。
我们必须保护稀缺资源。

definition_zh: 真正地；真诚地；名副其实地
definition_en: in a real and sincere way, not falsely
core_image: 一个人听到好消息时眼睛一下子亮起来
scene: 他真心为她的成功高兴。 He was genuinely happy about her success.
sceneCN: 这里 genuinely 是「真心地；真诚地」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他真心为她的成功高兴。

senses.title: Really, truly
senses.definition: used to stress that something is really true
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事确实是真的
senses.example: The meal was genuinely delicious.
senses.exampleCN: 这顿饭确实很好吃。
senses.why: The adverb strengthens a claim that something is real.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词强化「某事是真实的」这一说法。

senses.title: With sincere feeling
senses.definition: with feelings that are honest and not pretended
senses.definitionCN: 带着诚实而非假装的感情
senses.example: He was genuinely happy about her success.
senses.exampleCN: 他真心为她的成功高兴。
senses.why: A real feeling, like real gold, has nothing added.
senses.whyCN: 真实的感情就像真金，没有掺杂。

senses.title: True to the name
senses.definition: in a way that fully deserves the description given
senses.definitionCN: 以完全配得上所给描述的方式
senses.example: It was genuinely a once-in-a-lifetime trip.
senses.exampleCN: 那真是一生一次的旅行。
senses.why: What is genuine lives up to its label completely.
senses.whyCN: 真正的东西完全配得上它的标签。

intro.en: Genuinely is the adverb built from genuine and -ly.
intro.cn: genuinely 是由 genuine 加 -ly 构成的副词。

items.en: Genuinus meant natural or native.
items.cn: genuinus 意为天生的、本来的。

items.en: Genuine entered English meaning natural, not artificial.
items.cn: genuine 进入英语时意为天然的，而非人造的。

items.en: The adverb genuinely added the -ly ending.
items.cn: 副词 genuinely 加上了 -ly 后缀。

items.en: It came to stress that a statement is really true.
items.cn: 它逐渐用来强调某个说法确实为真。

items.en: It also came to describe sincere feelings.
items.cn: 它也开始形容真诚的感情。

note.en: Genuinely is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of truth and sincerity.
note.cn: 把 genuinely 与形近词以及表示真实、真诚的副词作比较。

entries.definition: in a soft and careful way
in a real or genuine way
in an honest and genuine way

normalIntro.en: Genuinely means with nothing faked and nothing hidden.
normalIntro.cn: genuinely 就是没有造假、没有隐藏。

normal.en: He was genuinely happy about her success.
normal.cn: 他真心为她的成功高兴。

normal.en: The meal was genuinely delicious.
normal.cn: 这顿饭确实很好吃。

normal.en: It was genuinely a once-in-a-lifetime trip.
normal.cn: 那真是一生一次的旅行。

normal.en: She was genuinely sorry for the mistake.
normal.cn: 她真心为这个错误感到抱歉。

normal.en: They are genuinely interested in our work.
normal.cn: 他们真正对我们的工作感兴趣。

abstract.en: What is genuinely felt needs no performance.
abstract.cn: 真正感受到的东西不需要表演。

abstract.en: Truth spoken once is louder than flattery repeated.
abstract.cn: 说一次真话，比重复奉承更响亮。

abstract.en: A real welcome is heard before any word is spoken.
abstract.cn: 真正的欢迎，在开口之前就听得见。

examples.en: He was genuinely happy about her success.
examples.cn: 他真心为她的成功高兴。

examples.en: The meal was genuinely delicious.
examples.cn: 这顿饭确实很好吃。

examples.en: It was genuinely a once-in-a-lifetime trip.
examples.cn: 那真是一生一次的旅行。

dict_mnemonic.text: genuinely 就是 genuine（真正的）加 -ly：genuinely interested 是「真正感兴趣」，genuinely sorry 是「真心抱歉」，用来强调不是客套。

root: 由 genuine（真正的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 genuinus（天生的、本来的）。

sensesIntro.en: Genuinely means really and truly, with sincere feeling, or fully deserving the description.
sensesIntro.cn: genuinely 意为确实、真心地，或完全名副其实地。

core.en: Saying or feeling something with nothing faked.
core.cn: 说或感受某事时没有任何虚假。

branches.en: A dish tastes better than its price suggests.
branches.cn: 一道菜比它的价格更让人惊喜。

branches.en: Eyes light up before a word is said.
branches.cn: 话还没出口，眼睛先亮了。

branches.en: A rare day lives up to its name.
branches.cn: 难得的一天配得上它的名字。

branches.en: Truth in a fact and truth in a feeling share one root.
branches.cn: 事实中的真与感情中的真同出一源。

branches.en: A sincere heart and a true label point the same way.
branches.cn: 真诚的心与真实的标签指向同一个方向。

intro.en: Genuinely is the adverb form of the genuine family.
intro.cn: genuinely 是 genuine 词族的副词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin genuinus meant natural or native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 genuinus 意为天生的、本来的。

items.example: He genuinely cares about the team.
The genuineness of the coin was checked.
items.exampleCN: 这枚硬币的真实性经过了检验。

items.example: He smiled ungenuinely at the news.
items.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，他假笑了一下。
这份副本看起来很逼真。
他貌似真实的镇定让他们稳住了。

items.example: A genuine-hearted offer is hard to refuse.
items.exampleCN: 真心实意的提议很难拒绝。
他们以真诚伙伴的身份见面。

latinEntries.exampleCN: genuinus 是 genuinely 的源头。

definition_zh: 传染；感染；污染；影响（他人情绪）
definition_en: to pass a disease to a person, animal or plant, or to make something impure
core_image: 看不见的细菌从一个人手上跳到另一个人身上
scene: 医院里最怕伤口被弄脏。 The wound became infected after the bandage fell off.
sceneCN: 这里 infect 是「使感染」（第 1 个义项：病菌进入体内）；句意是绷带掉了之后伤口被感染了。

pos.zh: 动词：传染；感染；污染；感染（情绪）

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「感染；传染」
加形容词后缀 -ious，义为「有传染性的」
加过去分词词尾，义为「受感染的」
加否定前缀 dis-，义为「给……消毒」

senses.title: To pass on a disease
senses.definition: to give a disease to a person, animal or plant
senses.definitionCN: 把疾病传给某人、动物或植物
senses.example: The virus can infect people through the air.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒可以通过空气传染给人。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to put in, and a germ put into a body is exactly an infection.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「放进去」，而病菌被放进身体就是感染。

senses.title: To make a wound impure
senses.definition: to let germs enter a cut so that it becomes diseased
senses.definitionCN: 让病菌进入伤口，使之发炎
senses.example: Wash your hands so you do not infect the cut.
senses.exampleCN: 洗手，免得让伤口感染。
senses.why: From an invisible thing put into the body, the word turns to the opening it enters.
senses.whyCN: 从被放进身体的无形之物，这个词转向它所进入的开口。

senses.title: To contaminate something
senses.definition: to make food, water or an object carry germs
senses.definitionCN: 使食物、水或物品带有病菌
senses.example: Raw meat can infect the tools used to cut it.
senses.exampleCN: 生肉会污染切它的工具。
senses.why: Anything that can carry a germ is said to be infected by it.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能携带病菌的东西，都可以说被它感染。

senses.title: To spread to computers
senses.definition: to put a harmful program into a computer or network
senses.definitionCN: 把有害程序放进电脑或网络
senses.example: A single email may infect a whole system.
senses.exampleCN: 一封邮件就可能让整个系统感染病毒。
senses.why: The medical sense is borrowed for computer viruses, which spread the same way.
senses.whyCN: 医学义被借给电脑病毒，因为二者的传播方式相同。

senses.title: To pass on a feeling
senses.definition: to make others share your mood, energy or idea
senses.definitionCN: 让别人分享你的情绪、活力或想法
senses.example: Her laughter infected the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑声感染了整个房间。
senses.why: Emotion also spreads without contact, so the word carries cheerfulness as well as germs.
senses.whyCN: 情绪也无需接触就会传播，于是这个词既带病菌也带欢乐。

intro.en: Infect comes from Latin inficere, to put into or taint, built on in- plus facere, to make or do.
intro.cn: infect 来自拉丁语 inficere（放入、沾染），由 in- 加 facere（做、使）构成。

items.en: Inficere meant to dip in dye or taint something by putting another substance in it.
items.cn: inficere 意为浸入染料，或通过加入别的东西而污染。

items.en: The past participle infectus meant stained or corrupted.
items.cn: 过去分词 infectus 意为「被沾染的、腐坏的」。

items.en: The verb reached French and then Middle English with the sense of tainting.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语进入中古英语，带着「沾染」的意味。

items.en: As medicine advanced, infect narrowed towards germs entering the body.
items.cn: 随着医学进步，infect 收窄为病菌进入身体。

items.en: The word was later borrowed for computer viruses and for spreading feelings.
items.cn: 近代它又被借用于电脑病毒与情绪传播。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the Latin facere family; the near-meaning group holds words for passing on disease.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁 facere 词族；近义组收传播疾病的词。

entries.definition: A disease caused by germs, or their entry.
Able to spread from person to person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有传染性的」。
形容词，义为「完美的」，同出拉丁 facere。
动词，义为「污染」，强调混入有害物。

entries.definition: To pass on a disease to others.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「传播」，强调传递过程。
动词，义为「消毒」，与 infect 相反。

normalIntro.en: The hooks build on in- plus facere, then attach the word to wounds, offices and laughter.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子建立在 in- 加 facere 之上，再把词与伤口、办公室和笑声相连。

normal.en: In- means in and facere means make, so infect is to put something into something else.
normal.cn: in- 表示进入，facere 表示使，所以 infect 就是把某物放进另一物。

normal.en: Disinfect adds dis-, so it does the opposite: taking the germs out.
normal.cn: disinfect 加了 dis-，所以作用相反：把病菌拿走。

normal.en: Infection and infectious come from the same verb with -ion and -ious.
normal.cn: infection 与 infectious 由同一动词加 -ion 与 -ious 而来。

normal.en: Be infected with is the fixed frame for catching a disease.
normal.cn: be infected with 是表示「染上疾病」的固定框架。

normal.en: The computer sense keeps the medical picture: a virus that copies itself.
normal.cn: 电脑义保留了医学画面：一个会自我复制的病毒。

abstract.en: Infection is invisible entry: nothing is seen, but everything is changed.
abstract.cn: 感染是无形的进入：什么都看不见，一切却都变了。

abstract.en: A mood can infect a room exactly as a germ infects a body.
abstract.cn: 情绪能感染一间屋子，正如病菌能感染一具身体。

abstract.en: The word is about putting in, and the harm comes from what got in.
abstract.cn: 这个词讲的是放进去，而伤害来自进去的东西。

examples.en: The doctor said the cut would infect if left open.
examples.cn: 医生说这个伤口敞着会长染。

examples.en: Two hundred people were infected with the virus.
examples.cn: 有两百人感染了这种病毒。

examples.en: The software can infect every computer on the network.
examples.cn: 这个软件能感染网络上的每一台电脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬费克特」——硬要费心克服的特种病菌，会不断传染。

root: 拉丁语 inficere（放入、沾染）= in-（进入）+ facere（做、使）；同族词有 infection、infectious、perfect。

sensesIntro.en: From the physical act of putting a taint into something, infect narrows to germs in a body, widens to contaminated objects, and is borrowed again for computer viruses and for feelings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把污物放进某物的具体动作出发，infect 收窄为身体里的病菌，扩展到被污染的物件，再被借用于电脑病毒与情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible germ passing from one hand to another.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见的病菌从一只手跳到另一只手。

branches.en: DISEASE LINE: the germ enters a living body.
branches.cn: 疾病线：病菌进入活体。

branches.en: WOUND LINE: the entry point becomes diseased.
branches.cn: 伤口线：入口处发炎病变。

branches.en: OBJECT LINE: food, water and tools carry germs.
branches.cn: 物件线：食物、水和工具携带病菌。

branches.en: MACHINE LINE: a virus enters a computer.
branches.cn: 机器线：病毒进入电脑。

branches.en: FEELING LINE: a mood spreads like an infection.
branches.cn: 情感线：情绪像感染一样传播。

intro.en: A Latin verb of putting in, whose family covers medicine, cleaning and computer security.
intro.cn: 一个表示「放入」的拉丁动词，其词族覆盖医学、清洁与电脑安全。

latinIntro.en: The root facere, to make, appears everywhere in English, from factory to effect and perfect.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 facere（做、使）遍布英语，从 factory 到 effect 与 perfect。

definition_zh: 征服；占领；征服的成果；赢得
definition_en: the act of taking control by force, or something gained in this way
core_image: 旧地图上一块地方被涂成了另一种颜色
scene: 老师用深色笔在旧地图上圈出被占领的地区。 The conquest of the city changed the whole region.
sceneCN: 这里 conquest 指「占领；征服」（第 1 个义项：以武力取得控制）；句意是占领这座城市改变了整个地区。

collocations.zh: 赢得某人的心；取得一次胜利

senses.title: Taking by force
senses.definition: the act of taking control of a place or people by force
senses.definitionCN: 以武力取得对某地或某群人的控制
senses.example: The conquest of the coast took many years.
senses.exampleCN: 占领这条海岸用了许多年。
senses.why: A land changes hands, and the map must be redrawn.
senses.whyCN: 土地换了手，地图就得重新画。

senses.title: Something won
senses.definition: a place, people or thing won in this way
senses.definitionCN: 以这种方式赢得的土地、人民或东西
senses.example: The island was his greatest conquest.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛是他最大的战果。
senses.why: What is taken becomes a possession with a name.
senses.whyCN: 被夺取的东西，会变成一件有名字的占有物。

senses.title: A personal victory
senses.definition: a person won over, especially in love, or a hard personal success
senses.definitionCN: 被赢得的人，尤指爱情上的俘获，或艰难的个人成功
senses.example: He treated the friendship as a conquest.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这段友情当成一次征服。
senses.why: The old military word is borrowed for victories of the heart.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老的军事词，被借来形容心上的胜利。

intro.en: Conquest comes from Old French conqueste, from Latin conquirere, to seek out and obtain.
intro.cn: conquest 来自古法语 conqueste，源头是拉丁语 conquirere，意为四处寻求并取得。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, and conquirere meant to obtain by seeking.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求，conquirere 意为通过寻求而取得。

items.en: The noun conquestus named what had been won.
items.cn: 名词 conquestus 指已经赢到手的东西。

items.en: Old French conqueste was used for lands won in war.
items.cn: 古法语 conqueste 用于指战争中赢得的土地。

items.en: English conquest first meant the act of winning by arms.
items.cn: 英语 conquest 最初指以武力赢取的行为。

items.en: It also came to mean the thing won, not only the act.
items.cn: 它也开始指被赢得的对象，而不只是行为。

items.en: The word now extends to victories in love and in personal struggle.
items.cn: 如今这个词也扩展到爱情与个人奋斗中的胜利。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin seek base quest-, and the meaning group names other kinds of win.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语寻求词基 quest-，近义组列出其他表示胜利的词。

entries.definition: an act of politely asking for something
a long search for something important
the person who wins a conquest
success in a battle or contest

entries.definitionCN: 重大而值得庆祝的胜利

entries.definition: the act of taking something by force

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a map repainted, then move to the spoils that are named and to a heart won like a city.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张被改画的地图开始，再到被点名的战果，最后到像攻城一样被赢得的心。

normal.en: Conquest is conquer turned into a noun, so it is the whole event in one word.
normal.cn: conquest 是 conquer 变成名词，用一词装下整件事。

normal.en: Think of a map where one colour spreads over another.
normal.cn: 想想地图上一种颜色盖住另一种颜色。

normal.en: The act is the fighting, and the conquest is the land you can point to.
normal.cn: 行为是打仗，而 conquest 是你能用手指出的那片土地。

normal.en: A conquest needs a flag, a name and a date.
normal.cn: 一次占领需要一面旗、一个名字和一个日期。

normal.en: Love also has its conquests, though no one draws a map.
normal.cn: 爱情也有它的战果，只是没人画地图。

abstract.en: Picture a pen changing one country's colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔改变了一个国家的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a key handed over at a city gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙在城门处被交出来。

abstract.en: Picture a name carved on a stone after the battle.
abstract.cn: 想象战后石头上刻下的一个名字。

examples.en: The conquest of the city took three months.
examples.cn: 攻占这座城市用了三个月。

examples.en: The old empire lived on its past conquests.
examples.cn: 这个古老帝国靠过去的战果维持。

examples.en: He saw the new friendship as a quiet conquest.
examples.cn: 他把这段新的友情看作一次安静的赢得。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conquest 记成 conquer（征服）加 st 名词尾：攻城这件事和攻下来的城池，都叫 conquest。

root: 源自拉丁语 conquirere（com 彻底 + quaerere 寻求）的名词形式，经古法语 conqueste 进入英语，指征服行为与被征服的成果。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of taking land, to the land itself, and finally to a victory won over a heart.
sensesIntro.cn: 从夺取土地的行为，到土地本身，最后到在人心上取得的胜利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map repainted in one colour after an army passes.
core.cn: 核心意象：军队走过之后，地图被重新涂成一种颜色。

branches.en: The core sense is the act of seizing control.
branches.cn: 核心义项是夺取控制权这一行为。

branches.en: The result sense points at the land or people now held.
branches.cn: 结果义项指向如今被占有的土地或人民。

branches.en: The personal sense borrows the military picture for love.
branches.cn: 个人义项把军事画面借给了爱情。

branches.en: The act and its prize are two halves of one story.
branches.cn: 行为与战利品是同一个故事的两半。

branches.en: In both cases something is won and then kept.
branches.cn: 两种情形里，都是先赢得某物，再把它留住。

intro.en: Conquest carries the Latin seek base quest-, from quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: conquest 带着拉丁语的寻求词基 quest-，源自动词 quaerere（寻求）。

latinIntro.en: The same seek base appears in request, quest and question.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个寻求词基也出现在 request、quest 与 question 中。

items.meaning: the winning of land or people
a sentence that asks for an answer
items.exampleCN: 他问了一个简单的问题。
他们打听了火车的情况。

definition_zh: 狂野地；失控地；极度地；胡乱地
definition_en: in an uncontrolled manner, and in informal use to a very great degree
core_image: 一匹没上缰绳的马，在空地上左右乱冲，方向完全不由人
scene: 那匹马突然甩开缰绳，在空地上左右乱冲，谁都拉不住。 The crowd cheered wildly as the team came out.
sceneCN: 这里 wildly 是「狂野地、失控地」（第 1 个义项：以无法控制的方式）；句意为人群在球队出场时狂热欢呼。甩开缰绳乱冲的马，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 狂野地；失控地；极度地；胡乱地

senses.title: Without control
senses.definition: in a way that shows no restraint or control
senses.definitionCN: 以毫无约束或控制的方式
senses.example: The crowd cheered wildly as the team came out.
senses.exampleCN: 球队出场时，人群狂热欢呼。
senses.why: The adverb simply reports the untamed quality as the manner of a verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是把「未驯服」的性质作为动作的方式报告出来。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: in informal use, used before adjectives to mean extremely
senses.definitionCN: 口语中放在形容词前，表示极度
senses.example: The first attempt was wildly successful.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次尝试大获成功。
senses.why: A wild horse goes much further than a tame one, so the word became a strong intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 野马比驯马跑得远得多，于是这个词成了强力的强调词。

senses.title: With great variation
senses.definition: used of numbers or opinions that differ by a very large amount
senses.definitionCN: 形容数字或意见相差极大
senses.example: Estimates of the cost vary wildly.
senses.exampleCN: 对成本的估计差别极大。
senses.why: The adverb measures how far apart things are, and the distance is stretched wide.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词度量事物相距多远，而这段距离被拉得很宽。

senses.title: Without aim
senses.definition: used of shooting, swinging or guessing done with no aim
senses.definitionCN: 形容射击、挥打或猜测没有瞄准
senses.example: He swung wildly at the ball and missed completely.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝球胡乱一挥，完全打空。
senses.why: A shot with no aim flies wild, and the adverb keeps that picture of an arrow off course.
senses.whyCN: 没瞄准的一击会乱飞，而副词保留了那支偏离轨道的箭。

intro.en: Wildly is wild plus -ly, and it grew from describing animals to describing voices, numbers and praise.
intro.cn: wildly 是 wild 加 -ly，其用法从描述兽类扩展到声音、数字与称赞。

items.en: Wilde described untamed creatures and empty land, and did not yet need an adverb form.
items.cn: wilde 描述未驯服的兽与空旷的土地，当时还不需要副词形式。

items.en: Wildliche appears for acting in a wild manner, first of movement and weather.
items.cn: 中古英语的 wildliche 表示以狂野的方式行动，最初用于动作与天气。

items.en: The spelling became wildly, and it described how people laughed, ran and shouted.
items.cn: 拼写变为 wildly，用来描述人如何大笑、奔跑与呼喊。

items.en: Before adjectives it became an informal intensifier, as in wildly popular.
items.cn: 放在形容词前，它成为口语中的强调成分，如 wildly popular。

items.en: It also came to measure disagreement, as in estimates that vary wildly.
items.cn: 它还用来形容意见分歧，如 vary wildly 的估计。

note.en: The first group gathers other wild- words, the second the adverbs that mean very much or with no control.
note.cn: 第一组收其他 wild- 词族成员，第二组收表示「极度」「失控」的副词。

entries.definition: Gladly, sharing a similar ending shape.
In a fast, anxious, out-of-control way.
To a very great degree, the neutral choice.
With violent force or strong feeling.

normalIntro.en: Wildly takes wild and adds the plain -ly, so its two jobs are manner and degree.
normalIntro.cn: wildly 就是 wild 加普通 -ly，所以它做两件事：方式与程度。

normal.en: Wild gives the horse, ly turns it into how the horse moves.
normal.cn: wild 给出那匹马，ly 把它变成马奔跑的方式。

normal.en: Wildly successful is the informal intensifier, stronger than very.
normal.cn: wildly successful 是口语强调，比 very 更强。

normal.en: Vary wildly measures a gap, not a gesture.
normal.cn: vary wildly 量的是差距，不是动作。

normal.en: Cheer wildly needs a crowd and a finished race.
normal.cn: cheer wildly 需要一群人，还需要一场比完的赛。

normal.en: Swing wildly means the bat went where the ball was not.
normal.cn: swing wildly 说明拍子挥到了球不在的地方。

abstract.en: See a horse loose at full speed across an empty field.
abstract.cn: 看见一匹脱缰之马在空地上全速乱冲。

abstract.en: Hear a cheer that goes on after the whistle.
abstract.cn: 听见哨声之后仍在继续的欢呼。

abstract.en: Feel a guess fly off the page and miss.
abstract.cn: 感觉一个猜测飞出纸面，落了个空。

examples.en: The dog ran wildly round the garden.
examples.cn: 那只狗在花园里狂乱地跑。

examples.en: The book was wildly popular among students.
examples.cn: 这本书在学生中极受欢迎。

examples.en: Prices here have fluctuated wildly this year.
examples.cn: 今年这里的价格剧烈波动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪的理」——歪道理讲得又急又乱，狂野地往外冒。

root: 古英语 wilde（未驯服）+ 副词词尾 -ly → 中古英语 wildliche → 现代英语 wildly；同族有 wild、wildness、wilderness。

sensesIntro.en: The word describes a way of moving without control, then a very high degree, then a wide difference, and finally a swing with no aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先描述失控的动作方式，再表示很高的程度，然后是很大的差别，最后是没有瞄准的一挥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horse loose with the reins dragging.
core.cn: 核心意象：一匹脱缰的马，缰绳拖在地上。

branches.en: The cheer branch: a crowd past the whistle.
branches.cn: 欢呼分支：哨声已过仍在喊的人群。

branches.en: The success branch: a first try that worked.
branches.cn: 成功分支：第一次就成的尝试。

branches.en: The estimate branch: prices far apart.
branches.cn: 估计分支：相差极大的价格。

branches.en: The swing branch: missing the ball completely.
branches.cn: 挥击分支：完全打空。

branches.en: The intensity branch: manner and degree in one word.
branches.cn: 强度分支：一词兼顾方式与程度。

intro.en: Wildly is a plain -ly adverb, and the suffix does nothing more than turn the untamed adjective into a description of how something happens.
intro.cn: wildly 是普通的 -ly 副词，后缀只是把「未驯服」的形容词变成「如何发生」的描述。

latinIntro.en: The base is native Germanic, so there is no Latin source; the Latin entries below give the borrowed adverbs of the same force.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目给出同等力度的借入副词。

definition_zh: 抑制；阻止；约束
definition_en: to stop someone or something from doing something, often by holding back
core_image: 一只被绳子拉住、想冲出去却被紧紧拽住的狗
scene: 看到朋友要发火，她努力抑制自己的怒气，没有回嘴。 Seeing her friend about to lose his temper, she tried to restrain her anger and said nothing back.
sceneCN: 这里 restrain 是「抑制」（第 1 个义项：克制自己的情绪或冲动）；句意：看到朋友要发火，她努力抑制自己的怒气，没有回嘴。

senses.title: Hold back a feeling
senses.definition: to control a strong feeling so that you do not act on it
senses.definitionCN: 控制强烈的情绪，不让它表现出来
senses.example: She could hardly restrain her excitement.
senses.exampleCN: 她几乎抑制不住自己的兴奋。
senses.why: The Latin source means to draw tight, so restraining an emotion is pulling it back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为拉紧，因此抑制情绪就是把它拽回去。

senses.title: Stop someone from acting
senses.definition: to stop a person or animal from moving or doing something
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人或动物移动或做某事
senses.example: Two guards restrained the man at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 两名保安在门口拦住了那个男人。
senses.why: Physically holding someone back is the most concrete form of drawing tight.
senses.whyCN: 从身体上拉住某人，是「拉紧」最具体的形式。

senses.title: Limit an activity
senses.definition: to limit the growth or force of something
senses.definitionCN: 限制某事物的增长或力量
senses.example: High costs restrain the growth of small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 高昂的成本限制了小公司的发展。
senses.why: A force held back is a force kept within limits.
senses.whyCN: 被拉住的力，就是被限制在界限内的力。

intro.en: Restrain comes from Latin restringere, to draw tight, through Old French restreindre.
intro.cn: restrain 经古法语 restreindre 源自拉丁语 restringere（拉紧）。

items.en: Stringere means to draw tight or bind.
items.cn: stringere 意为拉紧或捆绑。

items.en: Restringere adds re- and means to hold back.
items.cn: restringere 加上 re-，意为拉住。

items.en: Restreindre keeps the sense of checking.
items.cn: restreindre 保留了抑制的含义。

items.en: Restrain covers both feelings and physical force.
items.cn: restrain 兼指情绪与身体力量。

items.en: The word also limits growth and activity.
items.cn: 这个词也用于限制增长与活动。

note.en: Restrain is close to control, restrict and hold back.
note.cn: restrain 与控制、限制、拉住等词相近。

normalIntro.en: Restrain belongs with strict: both come from the idea of drawing tight.
normalIntro.cn: restrain 与 strict 同源：两者都来自「拉紧」的想法。

normal.en: To restrain yourself is to hold your feelings on a short rope.
normal.cn: restrain yourself 就是把情绪拴在短绳上。

normal.en: Restrain anger means keep it from coming out.
normal.cn: restrain anger 意为不让怒气出来。

normal.en: A law can restrain harmful behavior.
normal.cn: 法律可以约束有害行为。

normal.en: The adjective restrained describes quiet, controlled style.
normal.cn: 形容词 restrained 描述克制含蓄的风格。

normal.en: Compare restrict: restrict sets rules, restrain pulls back force.
normal.cn: 对比 restrict：restrict 制定规则，restrain 拉住力量。

abstract.en: Picture a kite string held tight in both hands.
abstract.cn: 想象双手紧紧拉住风筝线。

abstract.en: Imagine a gate held shut against a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被人抵住，挡住人群。

abstract.en: Think of a horse stopped by a firm hand on the reins.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手稳稳拉住缰绳让马停下。

examples.en: He restrained a smile during the serious speech.
examples.cn: 在严肃的讲话中，他忍住没有笑。

examples.en: The officers restrained the crowd from entering the site.
examples.cn: 警察阻止人群进入现场。

examples.en: Several factors restrain the company from expanding too fast.
examples.cn: 几个因素限制了公司过快扩张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ strain（拉紧）」——把冲动往回拉紧，就是抑制与阻止；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ stringere（拉紧）→ restringere（拉住）→ 古法语 restreindre → restrain，核心义「往回拉住、不让冲出」。

sensesIntro.en: Restrain first holds back a feeling, then physically stops someone, and finally limits growth.
sensesIntro.cn: restrain 先指压住情绪，再指从身体上拦住某人，最后指限制增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a taut rope stopping a dog from rushing ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绷紧的绳子拉住想冲出去的狗。

branches.en: An emotion is held back before it acts.
branches.cn: 情绪在行动之前被拉住。

branches.en: A person or animal is physically stopped.
branches.cn: 人或动物在身体上被拦住。

branches.en: Growth or force is kept within limits.
branches.cn: 增长或力量被限制在界限内。

branches.en: Holding someone back protects order.
branches.cn: 拉住某人维护了秩序。

branches.en: Physical force and social limits share the same pull.
branches.cn: 身体的力量与社会限制共享同一种拉扯。

intro.en: Restrain combines the Latin prefix re- with stringere, to draw tight.
intro.cn: restrain 由拉丁语前缀 re- 与 stringere（拉紧）组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere gives strict, strain and restrain the same tight core.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere 让 strict、strain 与 restrain 共享「拉紧」的核心。

items.exampleCN: re- 在 restrain 中表示往回。

items.example: Old French restreindre carries the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 restreindre 传递了这个词。

definition_zh: 有能力的；胜任的；合格的
definition_en: having enough skill or knowledge to do something properly
core_image: 工匠一手扶住木料，一手稳稳下刀，不多不少
scene: 新来的电工查了一遍线路，十几分钟就排除了故障。 She is competent enough to handle the job alone.
sceneCN: 这里 competent 指「有能力的；胜任的」（第 1 个义项：具备足够本领）；句意是她足以独立处理这项工作。

pos.zh: 有能力的；胜任的；合格的

senses.title: Skilled enough to do the job
senses.definition: having enough skill or knowledge for a task
senses.definitionCN: 具备完成任务所需的技能或知识
senses.example: She is a competent driver on mountain roads.
senses.exampleCN: 她在山路上是个称职的司机。
senses.why: The word asks one quiet question: can this person carry the task safely?
senses.whyCN: 这个词只问一个朴素的问题：这人能把事稳妥地担起来吗。

senses.title: Acceptable but not outstanding
senses.definition: good enough to be accepted, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 足以被接受，但算不上出色
senses.example: The report is competent but never exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告合格，却谈不上精彩。
senses.why: Once a bar is set, meeting it exactly can sound like faint praise.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了及格线，刚刚够到就会带一点勉强的称赞。

intro.en: Competent comes from Latin competere, which also meant to be fit for a task.
intro.cn: competent 来自拉丁语 competere，这个词也有「适合某项任务」的意思。

items.en: Petere meant to seek or to aim at.
items.cn: petere 意为追求或瞄准。

items.en: Competere could mean to be suitable for something.
items.cn: competere 可以表示适合某事。

items.en: Competens described a person equal to a duty.
items.cn: competens 描述能担起职责的人。

items.en: Old French competent kept the sense of being fit.
items.cn: 古法语 competent 保留了「合适、称职」的含义。

items.en: English competent settled into skill and legal fitness.
items.cn: 英语 competent 落在技能与法律资格两方面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds members of the compete family, and the meaning group ranks capable, qualified and merely skilled.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 compete 家族的成员，近义组分辨有能力的、合格的和只是熟练的。

entries.definition: having the right training or papers

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a steady knife, then move to the standard a task sets and to the mild praise of just meeting it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从稳稳的一刀开始，再走到任务设定的标准以及刚刚够格时那点温和的称赞。

normal.en: Competent shares a root with compete: you are fit for the task at hand.
normal.cn: competent 与 compete 同根：你对眼前这件事是够格的。

normal.en: Competent is about the bar, not about brilliance.
normal.cn: competent 说的是及格线，而不是出众。

normal.en: The noun is competence, and its opposite is incompetence.
normal.cn: 名词是 competence，反面就是 incompetence。

normal.en: A competent cook never burns the rice.
normal.cn: 一个称职的厨子不会把米饭烧糊。

normal.en: Competent at a task means you can be trusted with it.
normal.cn: competent at 一项任务，意味着这件事可以交给你。

abstract.en: Picture a knife following a pencilled line without slipping.
abstract.cn: 想象一刀顺着铅笔线走，没有偏。

abstract.en: Picture a driver checking the mirror before changing lanes.
abstract.cn: 想象司机变道前先看一眼后视镜。

abstract.en: Picture a bar just touched by a jumper's hand.
abstract.cn: 想象跳高者的手刚好碰到横杆。

examples.en: A competent mechanic can find the fault quickly.
examples.cn: 一个有能力的技工能很快找出故障。

examples.en: The team is competent at handling complaints.
examples.cn: 这个团队处理投诉很在行。

examples.en: Her work is competent rather than brilliant.
examples.cn: 她的工作合格，但算不上出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 competent 记成 com（一起）加 pet（追求）加 ent：追得上任务要求的人，就是有能力的。

root: 源自拉丁语 competere，本义是「足以相称、合乎要求」，后指具备足够本领的、胜任的。

sensesIntro.en: From having the skill a task demands, to just meeting the bar and no more.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拥有任务所需的技能，到刚好够上及格线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carpenter whose knife follows the line without slipping.
core.cn: 核心意象：工匠一手扶住木料，一手稳稳下刀，不多不少。

branches.en: Being fit for the task is the practical core.
branches.cn: 足以胜任任务是这个词务实的核心。

branches.en: Meeting the bar exactly can sound like faint praise.
branches.cn: 刚好够到及格线，听起来就像淡淡的称赞。

branches.en: Both senses measure a person against a standard.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是拿一个人去对照一个标准。

branches.en: Trust grows when skill can be relied on.
branches.cn: 本领可靠，信任才会生长。

branches.en: The second sense warns against stopping at good enough.
branches.cn: 第二个义项提醒人别停在「够用」上。

intro.en: Competent takes the Latin base compet- and the adjective ending -ent.
intro.cn: competent 由拉丁词基 compet- 加形容词后缀 -ent 构成。

latinIntro.en: The same base yields competence, competent and competition.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个词基产出 competence、competent 与 competition。

items.meaning: the ability to do something well
items.example: Her competence reassured the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 她的能力让整个团队安心。

items.meaning: a specific skill needed for a job
items.example: The job lists five core competencies.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作列出五项核心能力。

items.meaning: in a skilled and reliable way
items.exampleCN: 她称职地处理了这个案子。

items.meaning: not skilled enough for a task
items.example: An incompetent pilot is a danger.
items.exampleCN: 不称职的飞行员是一种危险。

items.meaning: lack of skill for a task
items.exampleCN: 报告把原因归为纯粹的不称职。
这次修理做得极不专业。

items.example: Managers need both technical and social competencies.
items.exampleCN: 管理者既需要技术专长，也需要社交能力。

definition_zh: 前夕；前夜；傍晚
definition_en: the day or evening before an important day
core_image: 重要日子前的那一晚，屋里已经挂好装饰，静静等待
scene: 除夕前夜，街上挂满了红灯笼，人们忙着准备年夜饭。 On the eve of New Year, red lanterns hung everywhere and people were busy preparing the holiday meal.
sceneCN: 这里 eve 是「前夜」（第 1 个义项：重要日子之前的那一天或那一晚）；句意：除夕前夜，街上挂满了红灯笼，人们忙着准备年夜饭。

senses.title: The day before
senses.definition: the day or night before an important event
senses.definitionCN: 重要事件之前的那一天或那一晚
senses.example: We arrived on the eve of the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在婚礼前夜到达。
senses.why: Eve is a worn-down form of even, an old word for evening.
senses.whyCN: eve 是 even 的磨损形式，而 even 是表示傍晚的古词。

senses.title: Evening
senses.definition: evening, used mainly in old or literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 傍晚，主要用于古老或文学性文字
senses.example: The fields were quiet in the summer eve.
senses.exampleCN: 夏日的傍晚，田野十分安静。
senses.why: The original sense was simply evening, and traces remain in poetry.
senses.whyCN: 最初的含义就是傍晚，这一痕迹仍留在诗歌中。

intro.en: Eve is a shortened form of even, Old English ǣfen, meaning evening.
intro.cn: eve 是 even 的缩短形式，源自古英语 ǣfen（傍晚）。

items.en: Ǣfen means evening.
items.cn: ǣfen 意为傍晚。

items.en: Even and eve both name the evening.
items.cn: even 与 eve 都指傍晚。

items.en: Eve comes to mean the night before a festival.
items.cn: eve 逐渐指节日之前的夜晚。

items.en: New Year's Eve and Christmas Eve fix the pattern.
items.cn: 除夕与平安夜固定了这一用法。

items.en: On the eve of also means just before an event.
items.cn: on the eve of 也指事件即将发生之前。

note.en: Eve is close to evening and to phrases marking the time before an event.
note.cn: eve 与傍晚相近，也用于标记事件发生前的时刻。

entries.definition: the time when day becomes night

normalIntro.en: Eve is the quiet evening that stands at the door of a big day.
normalIntro.cn: eve 就是站在重要日子门口的安静夜晚。

normal.en: New Year's Eve is the last night of the year.
normal.cn: New Year's Eve 是一年的最后一夜。

normal.en: Christmas Eve is the night before Christmas.
normal.cn: Christmas Eve 是圣诞节前夜。

normal.en: On the eve of an event means just before it.
normal.cn: 「on the eve of an event」意为事件即将发生之前。

normal.en: Eve is shorter than evening and feels older.
normal.cn: eve 比 evening 短，也更古老。

normal.en: Compare evening: evening is any evening, eve is usually the one before something.
normal.cn: 对比 evening：evening 泛指傍晚，eve 通常指某事之前的那一晚。

abstract.en: Picture a house decorated and waiting for morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一间装饰好、静静等待天明的屋子。

abstract.en: Imagine a stage set before the curtain rises.
abstract.cn: 想象大幕拉开前已经布置好的舞台。

abstract.en: Think of a candle lit on the last night of the year.
abstract.cn: 想象一年最后一夜点燃的蜡烛。

examples.en: The streets were crowded on Christmas Eve.
examples.cn: 平安夜街上很拥挤。

examples.en: On the eve of the exam, she reviewed her notes.
examples.cn: 考试前夜，她复习了笔记。

examples.en: The company changed direction on the eve of the launch.
examples.cn: 公司在发布前夕改变了方向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「eve」与 evening 开头相近——重要日子前的那一晚；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ǣfen（傍晚）→ 中古英语 eve，核心义「重要日子之前的傍晚与夜晚」。

sensesIntro.en: Eve first means the day or night before an important event, and keeps an older literary sense of evening.
sensesIntro.cn: eve 先指重要事件之前的白天或夜晚，并保留「傍晚」这一较古老的文学含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a decorated room waiting quietly for the next day.
core.cn: 核心意象：装饰完毕、静静等待次日到来的房间。

branches.en: The night before an event is the main sense.
branches.cn: 事件前夜是主要义项。

branches.en: The older sense of evening survives in literature.
branches.cn: 「傍晚」的旧义在文学中留存。

branches.en: The evening before a big day is both time and mood.
branches.cn: 大事之前的傍晚既是时间，也是氛围。

branches.en: Festivals give eve its most familiar use.
branches.cn: 节日给 eve 最常见的使用场景。

branches.en: On the eve of also marks a turning point.
branches.cn: on the eve of 也标记转折点。

intro.en: Eve has no prefixes or suffixes; it is a shortened Old English word.
intro.cn: eve 没有前缀或后缀，是古英语词的缩短形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the word is native Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，是古英语本族词。

items.example: Eves appears in fixed holiday phrases.
items.exampleCN: eves 出现在固定的节日短语中。

items.example: New Year combines with eve for the holiday.
items.exampleCN: New Year 与 eve 组合成节日名称。

items.example: Christmas combines with eve for the night before.
items.exampleCN: Christmas 与 eve 组合指圣诞前夜。

definition_zh: 失望；令人失望的人；令人失望的事
definition_en: the feeling of being let down, or a person or thing that causes it
core_image: 桌上摊着一张没中奖的票，旁边是一杯已经凉了的茶
scene: 他把那张票对折两次，塞进外套口袋，没有再看第二眼。 Her face showed pure disappointment.
sceneCN: 这里 disappointment 指「失望」（第 1 个义项：希望落空的心情）；句意是她脸上满是失望。

pos.zh: 失望；令人失望的人或事

senses.title: The feeling of a failed hope
senses.definition: the sad feeling that comes when something hoped for does not happen
senses.definitionCN: 所盼望的事没有实现时那种难过的心情
senses.example: Her face showed pure disappointment.
senses.exampleCN: 她脸上满是失望。
senses.why: The gap between the picture and the fact has to go somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 画面与事实之间的落差，总得有个地方放。

senses.title: A person who lets you down
senses.definition: someone whose behaviour fails the trust placed in them
senses.definitionCN: 行为辜负了别人信任的人
senses.example: He turned out to be a great disappointment to his teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他最终让老师大为失望。
senses.why: A person can carry the whole weight of a broken promise.
senses.whyCN: 一个人身上，能背着整个落空的承诺。

senses.title: A result that fails to satisfy
senses.definition: an event or result that is worse than what was expected
senses.definitionCN: 比预期更差的赛事或结果
senses.example: The concert was a disappointment from start to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 那场音乐会从头到尾都让人失望。
senses.why: Some things are remembered only for what they were not.
senses.whyCN: 有些事被人记住，只因为它没成为该有的样子。

intro.en: Disappointment is disappoint plus -ment, and its French source first meant removal from a post.
intro.cn: disappointment 是 disappoint 加 -ment，其法语源头本指免职。

items.en: Desappointer meant to remove a person from an appointment.
items.cn: desappointer 指解除某人的职位。

items.en: Disappointment first named the act of depriving someone of office.
items.cn: disappointment 最初指剥夺某人职位的行为。

items.en: The sense shifted to a hope or plan being defeated.
items.cn: 词义转向希望或计划受挫。

items.en: The word named the feeling that follows a failed hope.
items.cn: 这个词开始指希望落空之后的感受。

items.en: It also names the person or event that causes the feeling.
items.cn: 它也可指引起这种感受的人或事。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the disappoint stem, while the meaning group names related blows to hope.
note.cn: 形近组共用 disappoint 这一段词干，近义组则列出几种对希望的打击。

entries.definition: to fail to satisfy a hope
sad because a hope was not met
entries.definitionCN: 因希望未实现而难过的

entries.definition: a feeling of being let down by someone or something
the feeling of being blocked from a goal
a strong feeling of shock and loss of hope
entries.definitionCN: 震惊而失去希望的强烈感受

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a losing ticket to a person who carries a broken promise.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一张没中奖的票，走到背着一个落空承诺的人。

normal.en: Disappointment is disappoint turned into a thing you can hold.
normal.cn: disappointment 就是把 disappoint 变成一个能捧在手里的东西。

normal.en: To your disappointment, the ticket was blank.
normal.cn: 令你失望的是，那张票是空的。

normal.en: A concert can be a disappointment and still fill a hall.
normal.cn: 一场音乐会可能让人失望，却照样坐满大厅。

normal.en: A person can be a disappointment without being a stranger.
normal.cn: 一个人可能让人失望，却仍不是陌生人。

normal.en: The word names both the wound and the hand that made it.
normal.cn: 这个词既指伤口，也指弄出伤口的那只手。

abstract.en: Picture a ticket folded twice and pushed into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一张票被折两下，塞进口袋。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of tea gone cold beside an open letter.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯凉掉的茶放在拆开的信旁。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that closes like a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑像门一样合上。

examples.en: To my disappointment, the shop was closed.
examples.cn: 令我失望的是，那家店关门了。

examples.en: She could not hide her disappointment at the news.
examples.cn: 听到这个消息，她藏不住失望。

examples.en: The trip was a disappointment for the whole family.
examples.cn: 这趟旅行让全家都很失望。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disappointment 记成「的士破印门」：约好的的士没来，票上的印破了，门也关上了，只剩失望。

root: 由 disappoint 加名词词尾 -ment 构成。disappoint 出自古法语 desappointer（免职），词基 point 指位置。这个词先指剥夺职位的行为，十七世纪转向希望受挫，十八世纪又指希望落空后的心情，以及引起这种心情的人或事。

sensesIntro.en: From the ache of a failed hope, to the person who caused it, to the event remembered for falling short.
sensesIntro.cn: 从希望落空的酸楚，到造成它的人，再到因不如预期而被记住的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a losing ticket folded small and put away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张没中奖的票被折小收起来。

chain: A HOPE IS HELD UP HIGH

branches.en: The first sense is the feeling left by the gap.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那道落差留下的感受。

branches.en: The second sense is the person who made the gap.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是弄出那道落差的人。

branches.en: The third sense is the event that could not fill it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是填不上那道落差的事。

branches.en: The feeling and the person are named by one word.
branches.cn: 感受和人，共用同一个词。

branches.en: A hope and an evening can both end in the same quiet.
branches.cn: 一份希望和一个夜晚，可能收在同样的安静里。

intro.en: Disappointment belongs to the appoint family, words about posts, promises and hopes.
intro.cn: disappointment 属于 appoint 一族，围绕职位、约定与希望。

latinIntro.en: The base point descends from Latin punctum, a point or a fixed place.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 point 出自拉丁语 punctum（点、固定位置）。

items.meaning: the feeling of a failed hope
items.example: The disappointment was written on his face.

items.meaning: to fail to meet a hope
items.example: I hope the film will not disappoint you.
items.exampleCN: 希望这部电影不会让你失望。

items.meaning: in a way that lets people down
items.exampleCN: 这一天结束得早，让人扫兴。

items.meaning: to choose someone for a post
items.exampleCN: 他们任命了一位新经理。

items.meaning: a fixed meeting or a post
to choose someone for a post again
items.exampleCN: 董事会重新任命了那位主管。

definition_zh: 抗议；反对；规劝；告诫
definition_en: to protest strongly or to urge someone earnestly to change their behaviour
core_image: 一个人把证据摊在桌上，指着它要求对方收回决定
scene: 几位居民堵在工地门口，向负责人抗议夜间施工的噪音。 Several residents remonstrated with the site manager about the noise at night.
sceneCN: 这里 remonstrate 是「抗议、反对」（第 1 个义项：强烈地表达不满）；句意：几位居民就夜间噪音向工地负责人提出抗议。

derivatives.zh: remonstrate 加 -ance 构成，义为「抗议；谏言」
remonstrate 加 -ant 构成，义为「抗议的」

senses.title: To protest strongly
senses.definition: to tell someone forcefully that you think their action is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 有力地告诉对方，你认为其行为是错的
senses.example: The workers remonstrated against the sudden pay cut.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们抗议突然的降薪。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to show back, so the core picture is laying evidence before someone in order to push back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「反过来展示」，所以核心画面是把证据摆到对方面前以表示反对。

senses.title: To urge someone earnestly to change
senses.definition: to advise someone seriously and at length against a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 认真而持续地劝某人不要走某条路
senses.example: His friends remonstrated with him about leaving school.
senses.exampleCN: 朋友们劝他不要退学。
senses.why: Showing someone the reasons can be aimed at correcting them rather than merely objecting, which gives the advising sense.
senses.whyCN: 把理由摆给对方看，目的可以是纠正而不只是反对，由此生出「规劝」义。

intro.en: Remonstrate comes from Latin remonstrare, to show back, built on re- and monstrare, to show.
intro.cn: remonstrate 来自拉丁语 remonstrare「反过来指明」，由 re- 与 monstrare「展示」构成。

items.en: Monstrare means to show or point out, and gives demonstrate and monster.
items.cn: monstrare 意为展示、指出，产生了 demonstrate 与 monster。

items.en: Remonstrare adds re- and means to show in return or point out in opposition.
items.cn: remonstrare 加 re-，意为反过来指出或以指明的方式反对。

items.en: Remonstrare develops the legal sense of setting out a grievance.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中，remonstrare 发展出陈述申诉的法律义。

items.en: English remonstrate enters through French with the sense of making a formal protest.
items.cn: 十六世纪，remonstrate 经法语进入英语，带有正式抗议的含义。

items.en: The word splits into the public sense of protest and the private sense of earnest advice.
items.cn: 这个词分成公开抗议与私下规劝两个方向。

note.en: Remonstrate belongs to the monstrare family of showing, and to the vocabulary of protest and advice.
note.cn: remonstrate 属于 monstrare「展示」词族，也属于抗议与规劝的词汇。

entries.definitionCN: 抗议；谏书，由 remonstrate 加 -ance 构成

entries.definition: to show clearly by giving proof
entries.definitionCN: 证明；演示，与 remonstrate 共享 monstrare 词根
怪物，同出 monstrum「被指出之物」，但意义已远离

entries.definition: to say strongly that you disagree with something
entries.definitionCN: 抗议；反对，是最直接的近义词

entries.definition: to say that you disagree or disapprove
entries.definitionCN: 反对；提出异议，语气较弱

entries.definition: to warn or advise someone seriously
entries.definitionCN: 告诫；警告，与第二义项接近

normalIntro.en: The monstr- root of showing links remonstrate with demonstrate, so the word pictures evidence held up.
normalIntro.cn: 表示「展示」的 monstr- 词根把 remonstrate 与 demonstrate 连起来，画面是举起证据。

normal.en: Re- plus monstrare, to show, means showing something back in argument.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 monstrare「展示」，就是把东西反过来展示出来争论。

normal.en: Demonstrate shares the identical monstr- root and means showing forward.
normal.cn: demonstrate 共享完全相同的 monstr- 词根，表示正面展示。

normal.en: The verb is usually followed by with, against, or about.
normal.cn: 这个动词后常接 with、against 或 about。

normal.en: The noun remonstrance adds -ance and often sounds formal or historical.
normal.cn: 名词 remonstrance 加 -ance，常带正式或历史色彩。

normal.en: Remonstrate is stronger and more formal than complain.
normal.cn: remonstrate 比 complain 更强烈、更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a letter of complaint being placed on a manager's desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一封投诉信被放在经理的桌上。

abstract.en: See a crowd standing at a gate with signs held high.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人站在大门口，高举标语。

abstract.en: Think of a friend holding your arm and listing reasons not to leave.
abstract.cn: 想一位朋友拉住你的手臂，一条条列举不该离开的理由。

examples.en: She remonstrated with the driver about the speed.
examples.cn: 她向司机抗议车速太快。

examples.en: The elders remonstrated against closing the village school.
examples.cn: 长辈们反对关闭村里的学校。

examples.en: He was remonstrated with for missing so many meetings.
examples.cn: 他因缺席太多会议而被规劝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞蒙斯特雷特」——想象瑞丽有人拉着你讲道理，不许你走；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 remonstrare（re-「回、反」+ monstrare「展示」），字面即「反过来指明」，引申为抗议、规劝。

sensesIntro.en: Laying evidence in front of someone can either push back against them or lead them away from a mistake.
sensesIntro.cn: 把证据摆到对方面前，既可以用来抵制对方，也可以用来把对方从错误中引开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: evidence laid on the table and pushed toward the other person.
core.cn: 核心意象：把证据摊在桌上，推对方面前。

branches.en: Showing something back becomes public protest.
branches.cn: 把东西反过来展示，成为公开抗议。

branches.en: Showing reasons can also be an attempt to correct a friend.
branches.cn: 摆出理由也可以是试图纠正朋友。

branches.en: Both senses use evidence, only the goal differs.
branches.cn: 两个义项都用证据，区别只在目的。

branches.en: A public setting makes the protest formal and collective.
branches.cn: 公开场合让抗议变得正式且集体化。

branches.en: A private setting turns the same act into earnest advice.
branches.cn: 私下场合让同一个动作变成恳切规劝。

intro.en: Remonstrate is a Latin verb whose prefix and showing root are both still transparent.
intro.cn: remonstrate 是一个拉丁动词，其前缀与表示「展示」的词根仍然清晰可辨。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means back, and monstrare means to show, so the pair means to show in return.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「回、反」，monstrare 表示「展示」，两者合起来就是「反过来展示」。

items.example: Re- turns the showing into a counter-move.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 把展示变成一种反制动作。

items.example: The monstr- root also appears in demonstrate.
items.exampleCN: monstr- 词根也出现在 demonstrate 中。

items.example: Monstrare is the verb behind the root.
items.exampleCN: monstrare 是这个词根背后的动词。

items.meaning: marks a verb from a stem
items.meaningCN: 由词干构成动词的词尾
items.example: The ending -ate marks the English verb form.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 标记英语动词形式。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或行为的名词词尾
items.example: Remonstrance names the act of protesting.
Remonstrare is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: remonstrare 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.example: Demonstrate adds de- to the same monstr- root.
items.exampleCN: demonstrate 在同一个 monstr- 词根前加了 de-。

items.meaning: a structure that keeps a memory
items.example: Monument comes from monere, a close cousin of monstrare.
items.exampleCN: monument 来自 monere，与 monstrare 是近亲。

definition_zh: 爆炸；一阵强风；轰鸣；猛烈批评
definition_en: an explosion, or a sudden strong movement of air
core_image: 爆破瞬间扬起的尘土
scene: 远处山脚腾起一团灰白的烟尘。 The blast shook the windows of the town.
sceneCN: 这里 blast 是「爆炸」（第 1 个义项：突然的剧烈炸开）；句意是爆炸震动了镇上的窗户。

pos.zh: 名词：爆炸；一阵强风；轰鸣

derivatives.zh: 被炸毁的；该死的，用于加强语气
爆破，用炸药炸开岩石的作业

senses.title: A sudden explosion
senses.definition: a sudden violent burst of energy
senses.definitionCN: 突然而猛烈的能量爆开
senses.example: The blast shook the windows of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 爆炸震动了镇上的窗户。
senses.why: Gunpowder work gave the word this violent sense.
senses.whyCN: 炸药的作业让这个词有了这层猛烈的意思。

senses.title: A sudden rush of air
senses.definition: a sudden strong movement of air
senses.definitionCN: 突然而强劲的一股气流
senses.example: A blast of cold air hit us at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 一开门，一股冷风扑面而来。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from the idea of blowing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自「吹」这个概念。

senses.title: A very loud sudden noise
senses.definition: a sudden loud sound, as from a horn or trumpet
senses.definitionCN: 号角或喇叭发出的突然巨响
senses.example: The blast of the horn made her jump.
senses.exampleCN: 喇叭的巨响吓了她一跳。
senses.why: A horn blast is a burst of air made audible.
senses.whyCN: 号角声就是把一股气流变成了能听见的爆响。

senses.title: A strong attack in words
senses.definition: a very strong criticism
senses.definitionCN: 非常严厉的批评
senses.example: The film drew a blast from critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影招来评论家的猛烈批评。
senses.why: Verbal attack borrowed the force of an explosion.
senses.whyCN: 言语攻击借用了爆炸的力量感。

intro.en: Blast began as a word for blowing and later took on explosion.
intro.cn: blast 本指吹气，后来才获得爆炸的含义。

items.en: blæst meant a blowing of wind.
items.cn: blæst 意为一阵吹风。

items.en: blast named the sound of a trumpet.
items.cn: blast 指号角吹出的声音。

items.en: blasting with gunpowder gave the explosion sense.
items.cn: 用火药爆破让这个词有了爆炸义。

items.en: blast covered sudden loud noises of all kinds.
items.cn: blast 泛指各种突然的巨响。

items.en: blast also means a strong criticism.
items.cn: 如今 blast 也可指猛烈的批评。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bla- opening; the near-meaning group names explosions and gusts.
note.cn: 形近组都以 bla- 开头；近义组是爆炸与阵风类词。

normalIntro.en: Blast is a burst: of air, of sound, of fire, of words.
normalIntro.cn: blast 是一次爆发：气流的、声音的、火药的、言语的。

normal.en: A blast of wind is a sudden gust.
normal.cn: a blast of wind 是一阵突来的风。

normal.en: Blast off sends a rocket up.
normal.cn: blast off 指火箭发射升空。

normal.en: A bomb blast is an explosion.
normal.cn: a bomb blast 是炸弹爆炸。

normal.en: To blast someone is to criticize hard.
normal.cn: blast someone 是猛烈批评某人。

normal.en: Blast and blow share a root.
normal.cn: blast 与 blow 同根。

abstract.en: See dust rising from a hillside.
abstract.cn: 想象山坡上升起的尘土。

abstract.en: See a door blown open by wind.
abstract.cn: 想象门被风吹开。

abstract.en: See a trumpet at full volume.
abstract.cn: 想象一把吹到最响的小号。

examples.en: The blast shook the windows of the town.
examples.cn: 爆炸震动了镇上的窗户。

examples.en: A blast of cold air hit us at the door.
examples.cn: 一开门，一股冷风扑面而来。

examples.en: The film drew a blast from critics.
examples.cn: 这部电影招来评论家的猛烈批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: blast 与 blow 同源，一口猛吹是一阵狂风，吹得炸开就是爆炸。

root: blast 源自古英语 blæst，本义「一阵吹风」，与 blawan（吹）同根；中古英语指号角声，十七世纪火药爆破赋予爆炸义，后又引申为猛烈批评。

sensesIntro.en: Air, noise, fire and words can all come out in one blast.
sensesIntro.cn: 气流、声响、火药与言语，都可以是一次 blast。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dust thrown up by an explosion at a hillside.
core.cn: 核心意象：山脚爆破扬起的尘土。

branches.en: a bomb blast
branches.cn: 炸弹爆炸

branches.en: a blast of wind
branches.cn: 一阵强风

branches.en: the blast of a horn
branches.cn: 号角的巨响

branches.en: a blast from critics
branches.cn: 评论家的猛烈批评

branches.en: a blast of cold air
branches.cn: 一股冷风

intro.en: Blast makes an adjective and a noun with -ed and -ing.
intro.cn: blast 加 -ed 与 -ing 构成形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Old English; Latin items below are related in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古英语，下面的拉丁词只在意思上相关。

items.meaning: the work of blowing up rock

definition_zh: 实际的；事实上的；（计算机）虚拟的
definition_en: almost or in effect so, though not formally, and, in computing, created by software rather than existing physically
core_image: 戴上头显后，房间里凭空出现一张桌子
scene: 老师宣布这学期有几次课在线上进行，用的是一个虚拟教室。 The class met in a virtual classroom twice a week.
sceneCN: 这里 virtual 是「虚拟的」（第 3 个义项：由软件生成而非实物存在的）；句意为这门课每周两次在虚拟教室上课。戴上头显后凭空出现的桌子就是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 实际的；事实上的；虚拟的

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「几乎；实际上」
复合名词，义为「虚拟现实」
加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「虚拟性」

senses.title: In effect, though not in name
senses.definition: true in practice even if not officially so
senses.definitionCN: 事实上成立，但未获正式名义的
senses.example: The few shareholders hold a virtual monopoly.
senses.exampleCN: 少数股东握有近乎垄断的地位。
senses.why: Medieval Latin virtualis meant having a power or effect, and an effect can be real without a name.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 virtualis 意为具有效力，而效力可以真实却无名分。

senses.title: Almost, very nearly
senses.definition: so close to being so that the difference hardly matters
senses.definitionCN: 已经接近到差别几乎无关紧要
senses.example: There was a virtual absence of evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 几乎完全没有证据。
senses.why: If the effect is already there, the word can measure how near a thing is to being complete.
senses.whyCN: 效力既已存在，这个词便可以用来衡量事物接近完整的程度。

senses.title: Created by computer rather than real
senses.definition: made to exist by software, as a place or object on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 由软件生成、存在于屏幕中的场所或事物
senses.example: The class met in a virtual classroom twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课每周两次在虚拟教室上课。
senses.why: Software produces effects that feel real, which is exactly the old sense of the word in a new machine.
senses.whyCN: 软件产生了感觉真实的效力，正是这个词旧义在新机器中的化身。

senses.title: Existing in power but not in act
senses.titleCN: 潜在的；实质上的（哲学术语）
senses.definition: existing as a capacity that may become actual
senses.definitionCN: 作为一种尚未实现的能力而存在
senses.example: Scholastic writers spoke of the oak as virtual in the acorn.
senses.exampleCN: 经院学者说橡树潜在于橡子之中。
senses.why: The oldest philosophical use is about powers folded inside a thing.
senses.whyCN: 最早的哲学用法说的就是存在于事物内部的力量。

senses.title: Supported by software instead of hardware
senses.definition: of memory or storage, provided by software rather than by added hardware
senses.definitionCN: 内存或存储由软件提供而非增加硬件
senses.example: Virtual memory lets the computer run large programs.
senses.exampleCN: 虚拟内存让电脑能运行大型程序。
senses.why: A machine that has no extra chip can still behave as if it did.
senses.whyCN: 没有加芯片的机器也能表现得像加了芯片。

intro.en: Virtual descends from Latin virtus, power or worth, and first meant having that power in effect.
intro.cn: virtual 源自拉丁语 virtus（力量、价值），最初意为「在效力上具有该力量」。

items.en: Virtus meant strength, worth, and the power to act.
items.cn: virtus 意为力量、价值与行动的能力。

items.en: Virtualis described something that holds a power in effect.
items.cn: virtualis 形容在效力上持有某种力量的事物。

items.en: English virtual first meant effective, of a medicine or a power.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 virtual 最初指有效的，用于药物或力量。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it meant in effect but not in name.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，它表示「事实上如此但名义上不是」。

items.en: Computing added the sense of made by software in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪计算机领域又增添了「由软件生成」的含义。

note.en: The first group holds the virtue family, the second the words for real and nearly.
note.cn: 第一组是 virtue 词族，第二组是表示真实与几乎的词。

entries.definition: copied to look or feel real

normalIntro.en: Virtual and virtue share a root about power; what has the power of a thing counts as that thing.
normalIntro.cn: virtual 与 virtue 共有表示「力量」的词根；具有某物效力者便算作该物。

normal.en: Virtue, virtuous, and virtual all come from Latin virtus, power.
normal.cn: virtue、virtuous、virtual 都来自拉丁语 virtus（力量）。

normal.en: Virtual reality is real in effect but not in substance.
normal.cn: 虚拟现实在效力上真实，在实体上不真实。

normal.en: The adverb is simply virtual plus -ly: virtually.
normal.cn: 副词就是 virtual 加 -ly：virtually。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with virtual memory only: the word is older than computers.
normal.cn: 别只把它和虚拟内存挂钩，这个词比计算机古老得多。

normal.en: A virtual monopoly is one in fact, not by law.
normal.cn: virtual monopoly 指事实上的垄断，而非法律上的。

abstract.en: See a desk appear in an empty room once goggles go on.
abstract.cn: 想戴上眼镜后空房间里浮现出一张桌子。

abstract.en: Hear a class talking in a room that has no walls.
abstract.cn: 听一堂课在没有墙的房间里进行。

abstract.en: Think of an oak already folded inside a small acorn.
abstract.cn: 想橡树早已折叠在一颗小橡子里。

examples.en: The town has become a virtual ghost town since the factory closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，这座小镇几乎成了鬼城。

examples.en: Students attend virtual labs from home.
examples.cn: 学生们在家参加虚拟实验课。

examples.en: He is the virtual head of the department, though someone else has the title.
examples.cn: 尽管头衔在别人身上，他实际上是这个部门的主事人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃求尔」——沃师傅求来的那间屋，看着真，其实是屏幕里的虚拟屋。

root: 拉丁语 virtus（力量；德性）→ 中世纪拉丁语 virtualis（有效力的）→ 英语 virtual
