sensesIntro.en: One word about power becomes about effect, then about nearness, then about worlds made of software.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个关于力量的词先变成关于效力，再变成关于接近，最后变成关于由软件造出的世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk appearing in an empty room through goggles.
core.cn: 核心意象：透过眼镜在空房里浮现的桌子。

branches.en: The effect branch: a monopoly in fact, not in law.
branches.cn: 效力分支：事实上的垄断。

branches.en: The nearness branch: almost no evidence at all.
branches.cn: 接近分支：几乎没有证据。

branches.en: The screen branch: a classroom without walls.
branches.cn: 屏幕分支：没有墙的教室。

branches.en: The philosophy branch: the oak inside the acorn.
branches.cn: 哲学分支：橡子里的橡树。

branches.en: The machine branch: memory the computer borrows from disk.
branches.cn: 机器分支：电脑从硬盘借来的内存。

intro.en: The stem virt- means power or worth; -ual makes the adjective and -ly the adverb.
intro.cn: 词干 virt- 意为力量或价值，-ual 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin virtus gave Medieval Latin virtualis and English virtual, with virtue as a close cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virtus 派生中世纪拉丁语 virtualis 与英语 virtual，virtue 是近亲。

items.example: Virt- carries the idea of a working power.
items.exampleCN: virt- 携带一种起作用的力。

items.example: Virtual means relating to a power in effect.
items.exampleCN: virtual 意为与效力相关的。

items.example: Virtuality names the quality of being virtual.
A virtual win is not an actual one.
items.exampleCN: virtual 的胜利不等于 actual 的胜利。

items.example: A virtual ban is an effective ban.
items.exampleCN: 事实上的禁令就是有效的禁令。
模拟飞行用来训练飞行员。

items.example: Virtual reality is paired with real reality.
items.exampleCN: virtual reality 与真实现实相对。

definition_zh: 联合的；团结的；一致的；（诸国）联合而成的
definition_en: joined together or acting as one, especially in purpose
core_image: 一队人并肩拉着同一根绳
scene: 拔河那天下着雨，一队人也一步没退，绳子上的红布稳稳停在原地。 The team stood united to the end.
sceneCN: 这里 united 是「团结一致的」（第 1 个义项：作为一个整体行动）；句意为这队人始终团结到最后。并肩拉同一根绳，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词的原形动词，义为「联合」
同根名词，义为「联合；工会」
同根动词 unify 加后缀的名词，义为「统一；一体化」

senses.title: Acting as one body
senses.definition: working together with a single aim, without division
senses.definitionCN: 同心协力、没有分歧地一起做事
senses.example: The party remained united after the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票之后，该党依然团结。
senses.why: The past participle of unite tells you the joining is already done and now describes the body.
senses.whyCN: unite 的过去分词说明联结已经完成，如今用来形容那个整体。

senses.title: Formed by joining parts
senses.definition: made by bringing separate parts or areas into one organization or state
senses.definitionCN: 由分开的部分或地区合成一个组织或国家
senses.example: The United Kingdom was formed over several centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 联合王国是经几个世纪逐步形成的。
senses.why: A name that records the joining keeps the participle, as in the United Nations.
senses.whyCN: 记录这次联结的名称保留了分词形式，如 the United Nations。

senses.title: Held in common by a group
senses.definition: used to describe an effort or attitude shared by all concerned
senses.definitionCN: 形容所有相关方共同拥有的努力或态度
senses.example: They made a united effort to save the library.
senses.exampleCN: 他们共同努力保住了那间图书馆。
senses.why: What all share at once is exactly what makes a group one body.
senses.whyCN: 所有人同时拥有的，正是让一个群体成为一体的东西。

senses.title: Standing together despite pressure
senses.titleCN: 稳而不散的（应对压力时）
senses.definition: used when people hold together under attack or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 形容人们在受攻击或遇难处时仍然齐心
senses.example: The town stayed united through the hard winter.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇在艰难的那个冬天里始终不散。
senses.why: A body that does not come apart under strain shows the joining most clearly.
senses.whyCN: 在拉扯下不散的整体，最能显示那次联结。

senses.title: Joined in marriage or partnership
senses.definition: used formally of two people joined for life or for business
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法，指两人结为终身伴侣或生意伙伴
senses.example: The two architects have been united in one practice for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位建筑师多年来合开同一间事务所。
senses.why: The same image of one body applies to people who bind their lives or work.
senses.whyCN: 「一个身体」的意象，同样用在与他人结成生活或事业的人身上。

intro.en: The form is the past participle of unite, whose root is Latin unire, to make one.
intro.cn: 这个词形是 unite 的过去分词，其词根是拉丁语 unire（使成一体）。

items.en: Unire, from unus, meant to make one.
items.cn: unire 出自 unus，意为使成一体。

items.en: French developed the participle form that English later borrowed.
items.cn: 法语发展出分词形式，英语后来借入。

items.en: United appeared in English descriptions of joined groups.
items.cn: united 出现在英语中描写联合群体的文字里。

items.en: It became standard in names of states formed by union.
items.cn: 它成为由联合形成的国家名称中的标准用词。

items.en: The United Nations borrowed the same participle in 1945.
items.cn: 1945 年，联合国沿用了同一个分词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds unite family forms, and the near-meaning group covers harmony words.
note.cn: 形近组是 unite 词族的形式，近义组覆盖表示和谐的词。

entries.definition: a joining or a workers body

entries.definitionCN: 未被邀请的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The ending -ed says the joining is finished, so the word describes a body that is already one.
normalIntro.cn: 词尾 -ed 说明联结已经完成，因此这个词形容的是一个已经合一的整体。

normal.en: United is the past participle of unite used as an adjective.
normal.cn: united 是 unite 的过去分词作形容词。

normal.en: Stand united is the most common short pattern in speeches.
normal.cn: stand united 是演讲中最常见的简短说法。

normal.en: The United Nations and the United Kingdom record historic joinings.
normal.cn: 联合国与联合王国的名称记录了历史性的联合。

normal.en: A united effort means an effort shared by all.
normal.cn: a united effort 指所有人共同的努力。

normal.en: Unity is the state; united describes those who hold it.
normal.cn: unity 是状态，united 则形容拥有这种状态的人。

abstract.en: Picture a tug-of-war rope held by hands that do not shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被许多手握住、纹丝不动的拔河绳。

abstract.en: See a row of shields overlapping without a gap.
abstract.cn: 看一排盾牌交叠，没有缝隙。

abstract.en: Hear a vote called and answered by one voice.
abstract.cn: 听一次表决被同一个声音回应。

examples.en: The family stayed united after the factory closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关门后，这个家依然齐心。

examples.en: They presented a united front to the press.
examples.cn: 他们向媒体呈现出一个统一的阵线。

examples.en: The United Nations was founded in 1945.
examples.cn: 联合国成立于 1945 年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤奈替德」——尤奈是「一」，替德是「得到」，大家得到同一个心，就是团结。

root: unite 的过去分词，unite 源自拉丁语 unus（一）与 unire（使成一体），经古法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One finished joining describes a team, a shared effort, a name, a marriage, and a body under strain.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次已完成的联结，形容团队、共同付出、国名、婚姻与承压不散的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people pulling the same rope and not shifting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排人拉同一根绳，一步不退。

branches.en: The body branch: a group that acts without division.
branches.cn: 整体分支：没有分歧地行动的一群。

branches.en: The name branch: states and bodies formed by joining.
branches.cn: 名称分支：由联合形成的国家与机构。

branches.en: The effort branch: something all concerned share.
branches.cn: 努力分支：所有相关方共同之举。

branches.en: The strain branch: holding together through difficulty.
branches.cn: 压力分支：在难处中不散。

branches.en: The bond branch: two lives or firms joined formally.
branches.cn: 纽带分支：两种生活或两家机构的正式结合。

intro.en: A Latin root for one, a verb ending, and a participle ending make the whole word.
intro.cn: 表示「一」的拉丁词根、动词词尾与分词词尾，构成整个词。

latinIntro.en: Unire comes from unus, and unity and union are its close relatives.
latinIntro.cn: unire 出自 unus，unity 与 union 则是它的近亲。

items.exampleCN: 这些团体每年春天联合。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀

items.example: A harmonious choir is united in sound.
items.exampleCN: 和谐的合唱团声音如一。

definition_zh: 摄氏度（的）；百分度的
definition_en: relating to a temperature scale in which water freezes at zero degrees and boils at one hundred degrees
core_image: 把冰点到沸点均匀刻成一百格
scene: 冬天的早晨，窗上结了霜。 The thermometer showed five degrees centigrade below zero.
sceneCN: 这里 centigrade 指「摄氏度」（第 1 个义项：以冰点为零度、沸点为一百度的温标）；句意是温度计显示零下五摄氏度。

senses.title: The hundred-step temperature scale
senses.definition: a scale of temperature with zero at the freezing point of water and one hundred at the boiling point
senses.definitionCN: 以水的冰点为零度、沸点为一百度的温标
senses.example: Water boils at one hundred degrees centigrade.
senses.exampleCN: 水在一百摄氏度沸腾。
senses.why: The word says exactly what the scale does: a hundred equal steps from freezing to boiling.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把温标的做法说得很明白：从冰点到沸点均分一百格。

senses.title: Divided into a hundred degrees
senses.definition: describing any scale or instrument marked off in one hundred equal parts
senses.definitionCN: 形容任何被划成一百等份的刻度或仪器
senses.example: The old instrument had a centigrade dial.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧仪器有一个百分度刻度盘。
senses.why: Before it named a particular thermometer, the adjective simply meant hundred-stepped.
senses.whyCN: 在专指某种温度计之前，这个形容词只表示「分成一百格的」。

intro.en: Centigrade is a learned compound of Latin hundred and Latin step, naming a scale of one hundred steps.
intro.cn: centigrade 是拉丁语「一百」与「步、度」的学术复合词，指一百格的温标。

items.en: Centum meant one hundred.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centum 意为一百。

items.en: Gradus meant a step, a degree or a rank.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gradus 意为步、度或等级。

items.en: French centigrade was coined for a scale divided into a hundred degrees.
items.cn: 法语 centigrade 为分成一百度的温标而造。

items.en: English adopts centigrade as the thermometer with a hundred-step scale spreads.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语采用 centigrade，正值百格温标温度计推广。

items.en: Celsius is now the official name, while centigrade survives in everyday speech.
items.cn: 如今官方名称是 Celsius，centigrade 仍活在日常口语中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other centi- compounds, while the meaning group lists temperature scales.
note.cn: 形近组收其他 centi- 复合词，近义组列出温标名称。

entries.definitionCN: 身体细长、多足的爬行动物

entries.definition: the official name of the hundred-step scale
a scale with freezing at thirty-two degrees
entries.definitionCN: 冰点为三十二度的温标

entries.definition: a scale starting at absolute zero
entries.definitionCN: 从绝对零度开始的温标

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into hundred and step and link it to the freezing and boiling points.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词拆成「一百」和「度」，并把它与冰点、沸点连起来。

normal.en: Centi means hundred and grade means step, so centigrade is a hundred steps between ice and steam.
normal.cn: centi 意为一百，grade 意为度，所以 centigrade 就是冰与蒸汽之间的一百格。

normal.en: Centigrade and centimeter share the centi- prefix, both cutting a unit into a hundred parts.
normal.cn: centigrade 与 centimeter 共享 centi- 前缀，都把单位分成一百份。

normal.en: Degrees centigrade puts the scale after the number, as in five degrees centigrade.
normal.cn: degrees centigrade 把温标放在数字后，如五摄氏度。

normal.en: Celsius is the modern official name, but centigrade still appears in weather reports.
normal.cn: Celsius 是现代正式名称，centigrade 仍出现在天气播报里。

normal.en: The adjective never changes form, so there is nothing to add for plural or comparison.
normal.cn: 这个形容词没有形态变化，复数或比较都无需加词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a glass tube with a mark every hundredth of the way.
abstract.cn: 想象一根玻璃管，每百分之一的路程刻一道线。

abstract.en: Picture ice at the bottom mark and steam at the top mark.
abstract.cn: 想象底部刻度是冰，顶部刻度是蒸汽。

abstract.en: Picture a winter window with frost at minus five.
abstract.cn: 想象零下五度时结霜的冬日窗户。

examples.en: The room was about twenty degrees centigrade.
examples.cn: 房间大约二十摄氏度。

examples.en: Water freezes at zero degrees centigrade.
examples.cn: 水在零摄氏度结冰。

examples.en: The old thermometer is marked in centigrade.
examples.cn: 这支旧温度计按摄氏度刻度。

dict_mnemonic.text: centi 是一百，grade 是度：把冰到沸之间分成一百度，就是 centigrade。

root: 由拉丁语 centum（一百）与 gradus（步、度）复合而成，经法语 centigrade 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The literal hundred steps give the temperature scale, and the same compound describes any dial divided the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 字面的一百格给出温标义，同一复合词也形容任何如此划分的刻度盘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tube marked off into one hundred equal steps.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根刻成一百等份的管子。

branches.en: The hundred-step scale fixes zero at freezing and a hundred at boiling.
branches.cn: 百格温标把零度定在冰点、一百度定在沸点。

branches.en: Any instrument with a hundred divisions can take the adjective.
branches.cn: 任何分成一百格的仪器都能用这个形容词。

branches.en: Both senses come straight from the two Latin parts of the word.
branches.cn: 两个义项都直接来自这个词的两个拉丁成分。

branches.en: Celsius now carries the official name for the same scale.
branches.cn: Celsius 如今是同一温标的正式名称。

branches.en: The adjective sense is older and more general than the thermometer.
branches.cn: 形容词义比温度计义更古老、更宽泛。

intro.en: Centigrade is built from two Latin roots and shares the centi- prefix with many metric words.
intro.cn: centigrade 由两个拉丁词根构成，并与许多公制词共享 centi- 前缀。

latinIntro.en: Centum, hundred, and gradus, step, are the two elements of the compound.
latinIntro.cn: centum（一百）与 gradus（步、度）是这个复合词的两个成分。

items.example: The dose is a few centigrams.
The crack is two centimeters wide.
A centipede ran under the stone.

items.meaning: the official name of the scale
items.exampleCN: 科学界用 Celsius 取代了 centigrade。

latinEntries.exampleCN: centum 给出 centi- 前缀。
gradus 给出 grade 与 degree。

definition_zh: 影响；统治；摇摆
definition_en: to influence opinion or rule, or to move slowly from side to side
core_image: 树枝在风中缓缓摆动，讲台前的人正改变听众的想法
scene: 他的演讲影响了在场许多人的看法。 His speech swayed the views of many people present.
sceneCN: 这里 sway 是「影响」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的演讲影响了在场许多人的看法。

senses.title: To influence opinion
senses.definition: to change or guide someone's opinion or decision
senses.definitionCN: 改变或引导某人的意见或决定
senses.example: His speech swayed the views of many people present.
senses.exampleCN: 他的演讲影响了在场许多人的看法。
senses.why: This is the common sense of persuasion.
senses.whyCN: 这是「说服」的常见义项。

senses.title: To move from side to side
senses.definition: to move slowly back and forth
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢地来回移动
senses.example: The branches swayed in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 树枝在风中摇摆。
senses.why: This is the physical root sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理上的根源义项。

senses.title: Power or rule
senses.definition: control or influence over people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的控制或影响力
senses.example: The old law still holds sway in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧法在村里仍占支配地位。
senses.why: As a noun it names the power to move people.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时指左右他人的力量。

intro.en: Sway probably came from an old Norse word meaning to bend.
intro.cn: sway 可能来自古诺尔斯语中表示「弯曲」的词。

items.en: A root for bending or turning stood behind the word.
items.cn: 一个表示弯曲或转动的词根藏在词后。

items.en: Sveigja meant to bend or sway.
items.cn: sveigja 意为弯曲或摇摆。

items.en: Sway meant to move or rule.
items.cn: sway 意为移动或统治。

items.en: Sway extended to influencing opinion.
items.cn: sway 扩展到影响意见。

items.en: Hold sway became a fixed phrase for power.
items.cn: hold sway 成为表示权力的固定短语。

note.en: Sway is compared with look-alike words and with words for influence.
note.cn: 把 sway 与形近词以及表示影响的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sway is the movement that turns a body or a mind.
normalIntro.cn: sway 是让身体或心思转向的运动。

normal.en: His speech swayed the views of many people present.
normal.cn: 他的演讲影响了在场许多人的看法。

normal.en: The branches swayed in the wind.
normal.cn: 树枝在风中摇摆。

normal.en: The old law still holds sway in the village.
normal.cn: 这条旧法在村里仍占支配地位。

normal.en: She was not easily swayed by praise.
normal.cn: 她不容易被赞美左右。

normal.en: The boat swayed gently on the water.
normal.cn: 船在水面上轻轻摇摆。

abstract.en: Sway is both a body losing balance and a mind changing course.
abstract.cn: sway 既是身体失去平衡，也是心思改变方向。

abstract.en: To hold sway is to be the wind others bend to.
abstract.cn: 占支配地位就是成为他人顺应的风。

abstract.en: Persuasion is a quiet kind of swaying.
abstract.cn: 说服是一种安静的摇摆。

examples.cn: 他的演讲影响了在场许多人的看法。

examples.en: She was not easily swayed by praise.
examples.cn: 她不容易被赞美左右。

dict_mnemonic.note: 义项记忆 · 摇摆 → 影响 → 统治
dict_mnemonic.text: sway 本指物体来回摇摆，引申为使人「动摇、转向」，即影响，再引申为支配、统治。

root: 可能源自古诺尔斯语 sveigja（弯曲），经中古英语进入英语，由摇摆引申为影响与支配。

sensesIntro.en: Sway means to influence opinion, to move side to side, or to hold power.
sensesIntro.cn: sway 指影响意见、来回摇摆，或掌握支配力。

core.en: A movement that turns something.
core.cn: 让某物转向的运动。

branches.en: His speech swayed the views of many people present.
branches.cn: 他的演讲影响了在场许多人的看法。

branches.en: She was not easily swayed by praise.
branches.cn: 她不容易被赞美左右。

branches.en: The branches swayed in the wind.
branches.cn: 树枝在风中摇摆。

branches.en: The old law still holds sway in the village.
branches.cn: 这条旧法在村里仍占支配地位。

branches.en: Trees and opinions sway in the same word.
branches.cn: 树与意见在同一个词里摇摆。

intro.en: Sway forms swayed, swaying, and the noun swayer.
intro.cn: sway 可构成 swayed、swaying 与名词 swayer。

latinIntro.en: Sway is Germanic; its old form is closer to Norse than to Latin.
latinIntro.cn: sway 属于日耳曼语，其古老形式更接近诺尔斯语而非拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 摇摆的树看起来很平静。

items.example: The swayer of opinion spoke last.
items.exampleCN: 影响舆论的人最后发言。

latinEntries.example: Sveigja is the likely source of sway.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sveigja 可能是 sway 的来源。

definition_zh: 非凡地；显著地；出乎意料地
definition_en: in a way that is unusual and surprising, or to a surprising degree
core_image: 所有数字都很平常，唯独一栏高得刺眼
scene: 这个孩子只练了半年，就已经能完整弹下那首曲子。 For a child who had practised for only six months, she played the piece remarkably well.
sceneCN: 这里 remarkably 是「出乎意料地」（第 2 个义项：达到令人惊讶的程度）；句意：对一个只练了半年的孩子来说，她把这首曲子弹得惊人地好。

pos.zh: 非凡地；显著地；出乎意料地

derivatives.zh: remarkably 的形容词来源，义为「非凡的」
该词族的动词基础，义为「评论；注意到」

senses.title: In an unusual and striking way
senses.definition: in a way that stands out from what is normal and deserves attention
senses.definitionCN: 以超越常态、值得注意的方式
senses.example: The old engine ran remarkably smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧发动机运转得异常平稳。
senses.why: The adverb simply carries the adjective meaning into how an action is done, so the action itself becomes worth remarking on.
senses.whyCN: 副词只是把形容词的意思转移到动作的方式上，于是这个动作本身变得值得一说。

senses.title: To a surprising degree
senses.definition: used to say that an amount or level is much greater or smaller than expected
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明数量或程度比预期大得多或小得多
senses.example: Remarkably few people came to the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 来开会的人少得令人惊讶。
senses.why: When the size of something breaks expectation, the comment that follows is a comment on degree, which is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 当事物的量突破预期，随之而来的评论就是针对程度的，这就是第二义项。

intro.en: Remarkably is remarkable plus the adverb ending -ly, and the whole family goes back to the French verb remarquer.
intro.cn: remarkably 由 remarkable 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，整族词可追溯到法语动词 remarquer。

items.en: Remarquer means to mark, to notice, and later to comment.
items.cn: remarquer 表示做记号、注意，后来也表示评论。

items.en: The adjective remarkable is formed from remark with -able.
items.cn: 形容词 remarkable 由 remark 加 -able 构成。

items.en: The adverb remarkably appears soon after, adding -ly to the adjective.
items.cn: 副词 remarkably 随后出现，在形容词后加上 -ly。

items.en: Remarkably begins to work as an intensifier before adjectives such as well and little.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，remarkably 开始用在 well、little 等形容词前起强调作用。

items.en: Today it most often signals a surprising degree in reporting and description.
items.cn: 今天它最常用于报道与描写中，标示一种令人惊讶的程度。

note.en: Remarkably is the adverb of the remark family, and it stands near other degree adverbs.
note.cn: remarkably 是 remark 词族的副词，与其它程度副词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 非凡的；值得注意的，是 remarkably 的形容词

entries.definition: in an ordinary way that draws no attention
entries.definitionCN: 平淡无奇地，由否定前缀 un- 构成
评论；注意到，是该词族的动词

entries.definition: in a way that is very noticeable
entries.definitionCN: 显著地；惊人地，强调视觉冲击

entries.definition: especially, in a way worth noting
in a way that is unexpected
entries.definitionCN: 出乎意料地，侧重与预期相反

normalIntro.en: Remarkably is built in three steps from remark, so the hooks follow the endings.
normalIntro.cn: remarkably 从 remark 分三步构成，记忆钩子顺着词尾走。

normal.en: Remark, then remarkable, then remarkably: verb, adjective, adverb.
normal.cn: remark、remarkable、remarkably，依次是动词、形容词、副词。

normal.en: The ending -ly marks an adverb, so remarkably describes how something is done.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 标记副词，所以 remarkably 描述事情是「怎样」做的。

normal.en: It often intensifies well, similar, few, and little.
normal.cn: 它常用来强化 well、similar、few、little 这类词。

normal.en: Remarkably few is a common way to report a surprisingly small number.
normal.cn: remarkably few 是报道「数量少得惊人」的常用说法。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with remark, which is a verb or a countable noun.
normal.cn: 不要与 remark 混淆，后者是动词或可数名词。

abstract.en: Picture a bar chart where one column shoots above all the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一张柱状图，其中一根柱子高过其它所有柱子。

abstract.en: See a small child lifting a case twice her size.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小女孩提起比她大一倍的箱子。

abstract.en: Think of a clock that runs without a single second of error.
abstract.cn: 想一只一秒都不差的钟。

examples.en: The two designs are remarkably similar.
examples.cn: 这两个设计惊人地相似。

examples.en: She recovered remarkably quickly after the surgery.
examples.cn: 手术之后她恢复得异常迅速。

examples.en: Remarkably, no one was hurt in the crash.
examples.cn: 令人惊讶的是，撞车事故里没有人受伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞马克伯利」——想象马克伯在瑞丽的表现好得让所有人回头；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 由 remarkable 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，词根可追至法语 remarquer「做记号、注意」。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb either describes how something stands out or measures how far a quantity departs from expectation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词要么描述某事如何突出，要么衡量某个量偏离预期的程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one column in a chart towering over the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：图表中一根柱子高出其余所有。

branches.en: Doing something in a marked way is the qualitative sense.
branches.cn: 以带标记的方式做事，是性质层面的义项。

branches.en: Measuring how far a figure departs from expectation is the quantitative sense.
branches.cn: 衡量数字偏离预期多远，是程度层面的义项。

branches.en: Both turn a mental mark into a spoken emphasis.
branches.cn: 两者都把心里的标记转化为口头强调。

branches.en: Degree adverbs often sit right before the word they measure.
branches.cn: 程度副词常紧贴它所修饰的词之前。

branches.en: The manner sense usually follows the verb it describes.
branches.cn: 方式义通常跟在它所描述的动词之后。

intro.en: Remarkably carries the mark root plus an adjective ending and then an adverb ending.
intro.cn: remarkably 携带 mark 词根，并依次加上形容词词尾和副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The -able ending comes from Latin and the -ly ending is native English, so the word mixes two layers.
latinIntro.cn: -able 词尾来自拉丁语，-ly 词尾是英语本族成分，因此这个词混合了两层来源。

items.example: Re- strengthens the marking in the base word.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 强化了基础词中的标记动作。

items.example: The mark root is visible in marker and landmark.
items.exampleCN: mark 词根在 marker 与 landmark 中清晰可见。
remarkable 意为「值得被谈论的」。

items.example: The ending -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.example: Unremarkably means in a way that draws no notice.
items.exampleCN: unremarkably 表示「不引人注意地」。

items.example: Marquer lies at the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: marquer 位于整个词族的底层。

items.meaning: a sign or tool that marks
items.example: Marker joins the mark root with -er.
items.exampleCN: marker 把 mark 词根与 -er 组合。

items.example: Remarkable is the adjective immediately behind the adverb.
items.exampleCN: remarkable 是这个副词直接依托的形容词。
